title: 2001 : A Space Odyssey
description: Warner Bros. Pictures present an ‘unrestored’ 70mm print of the director’s groundbreaking science fiction epic! "For the first time since the original release, this 70mm print was struck from new printing elements made from the original camera negative. This is a true photochemical film recreation. There are no digital tricks, remastered effects, or revisionist edits. This is the unrestored film - that recreates the cinematic event that audiences experienced fifty years ago." - Christopher Nolan Stanley Kubrick’s dazzling, Academy Award®-winning* achievement is a compelling drama of man vs. machine, a stunning meld of music and motion. Kubrick (who co-wrote the screenplay with Arthur C. Clarke) first visits our prehistoric ape-ancestry past, then leaps millennia (via one of the most mind-blowing jump cuts ever) into colonized space, and ultimately whisks astronaut Bowman (Keir Dullea) into uncharted space, perhaps even into immortality. “Open the pod bay doors, HAL.” Let an awesome journey unlike any other begin. title: The Godfather Coda : The Death of Michael Corleone
description: As Michael Corleone (Al Pacino) ages, he finds that being the head of the Corleone crime family isn't getting any easier. He wants his family out of the Mafia, but the mob kingpin (Eli Wallach) isn't eager to let one of the most powerful and wealthy families go legit. Making matters even worse is Michael's nephew, Vincent (Andy Garcia). Not only does Vincent want a piece of the Corleone family's criminal empire, but he also wants Michael's daughter, Mary (Sofia Coppola).

title: I Want Your Sex
description: Gregg Araki's I Want Your Sex tells the story of Elliot (Cooper Hoffman), a kind-hearted if unmotivated twentysomething whose fantasies quickly come true when he lands a job with renowned artist and provocateur Erika Tracy (Olivia Wilde). When Erika breaks down office boundaries and takes Elliot on as her sexual muse and subordinate, their sexually charged relationship makes him question his own desires, boundaries, and relationships with his uptight girlfriend (Charli XCX) and repressed roommate (Chase Sui Wonders). As the stakes heighten and power dynamics shift, the film mixes satire, romantic comedy, mystery, and murder through the colourful and edgy visual language for which Araki is best known.

description: Pedro Almodóvar is back with his unique brand of storytelling, setting the stage for the tale of a filmmaker who is a little too heavily inspired by the real lives of those around him.

title: Notting Hill
description: The Electric's favourite rom-com returns - William Thacker (Hugh Grant) is a London bookstore owner whose humdrum existence is thrown into romantic turmoil when famous American actress Anna Scott (Julia Roberts) appears in his shop. A chance encounter over spilled orange juice leads to a kiss that blossoms into a full-blown affair. As the average bloke and glamorous movie star draw closer and closer together, they struggle to reconcile their radically different lifestyles in the name of love.

title: THE END OF EVANGELION
description: SEELE plans an attack on NERV after failing to create a man-made Third Impact. After reaffirming both her own and her mother’s existence in a state of despair, Asuka returns and begins the counterattack. However, new enemies descend from the heavens. Meanwhile, Shinji witnesses the horrifying wreckage of Asuka’s EVA-02 while piloting EVA-01. Mass production models surround EVA-01 and perform a solemn ceremony. What does it mean to complete a human heart?

title: The Invite             / Bob & Carol & Ted & Alice
description: Joe and Angela’s marriage is on thin ice. When they invite their enigmatic upstairs neighbors for a dinner party, the night spirals into unexpected places. Have they reignited the spark or lit the match that burns it all down? (A24)

title: Ghost Dog: The Way of the Samurai
description: An African-American Mafia hit man who models himself after the samurai of ancient Japan finds himself targeted for death by the mob.

title: Paprika
description: When a machine that allows therapists to enter their patients' dreams is stolen, all hell breaks loose. Only a young female therapist, Paprika, can stop it.

title: Andrei Rublev
description: Tracing the life of a renowned icon painter, the second feature by Andrei Tarkovsky vividly conjures the murky world of medieval Russia. This dreamlike and remarkably tactile film follows Andrei Rublev as he passes through a series of poetically linked scenes—snow falls inside an unfinished church, naked pagans stream through a thicket during a torchlit ritual, a boy oversees the clearing away of muddy earth for the forging of a gigantic bell—gradually emerging as a man struggling mightily to preserve his creative and religious integrity. Appearing here in the director's preferred 183-minute cut as well as the version that was originally suppressed by Soviet authorities, the masterwork Andrei Rublev is one of Tarkovsky's most revered films, an arresting meditation on art, faith, and endurance.

title: Monkey Business
description: Dr. Barnaby Fulton (Cary Grant) is a scatterbrained chemist working to create an elixir of youth. When one of his chimpanzees, Esther, breaks loose, she mixes chemicals in Barnaby’s lab, dumping the concoction into the office’s water cooler. The formula generates the rejuvenation effect Barnaby has been seeking — along with more chaotic side effects in some cases. Monkey Business allowed Monroe, who co-stars as Lois Laurel, to showcase her brilliant timing, further solidifying her reputation as a comedic actress.
director: Howard Hawks PRODUCED BY: Sol C. Siegel

title: Do The Right Thing
description: Salvatore "Sal" Fragione is the Italian owner of a pizzeria in Brooklyn. A neighborhood local, Buggin' Out, becomes upset when he sees that the pizzeria's Wall of Fame exhibits only Italian actors. Buggin' Out believes a pizzeria in a black neighborhood should showcase black actors, but Sal disagrees. The wall becomes a symbol of racism and hate to Buggin' Out and to other people in the neighborhood, and tensions rise.

title: Going Home
description: Going Home. 1972. USA. Directed by Adolfas Mekas. 16mm. 60 min. Reminiscences of a Journey to Lithuania. 1972. UK/West Germany. Directed by Jonas Mekas. 16mm. 81 min. Twenty-seven years after emigrating to the United States as refugees, Adolfas and Jonas Mekas returned to Semeniškiai, the Lithuanian village where they were born, to reunite with their mother and brothers before visiting the German labor camp where Adolfas and Jonas had been imprisoned during World War II. Going Home and Reminiscences of a Journey to Lithuania, shot by Adolfas and Jonas, respectively, remain among the most moving film diaries about exile and the ability of moving images to convey what is gained and lost amid the relentless passage of time and the cruel politics of displacement.

title: The Thing
description: In remote Antarctica, a group of American research scientists are disturbed at their base camp by a helicopter shooting at a sled dog. When they take in the dog, it brutally attacks both human beings and canines in the camp and they discover that the beast can assume the shape of its victims. A resourceful helicopter pilot (Kurt Russell) and the camp doctor (Richard Dysart) lead the camp crew in a desperate, gory battle against the vicious creature before it picks them all off, one by one.

title: DRACULA IN ISTANBUL
description:
A young lawyer travels from Istanbul to Romania to complete a legal transaction with the mysterious Count Dracula, despite warnings about his host's sinister reputation. After returning home, he discovers that Dracula has followed him to Istanbul, where the Count begins preying on those closest to him, prompting a desperate effort to stop the vampire before more lives are lost.
While closely following the broad outline of Bram Stoker's novel, the film relocates the action to contemporary Turkey and adapts the story through Ali Rıza Seyfi's unauthorized 1928 novel Kazıklı Voyvoda. It is notable for introducing several elements that later became closely associated with Dracula on screen, including prominent fangs and the Count scaling the walls of his castle.

title: UNIONDOCS PRESENTS: WELFARE
description: Frederick Wiseman’s WELFARE (1975) depicts the nature and complexity of the welfare system in sequences illustrating the staggering diversity of problems that constitute welfare: housing, unemployment, divorce, medical and psychiatric problems, abandoned and abused children, and the elderly. These issues are presented in a context where welfare workers as well as clients struggle to cope with and interpret the laws and regulations that govern their work and life. We’re excited to be partnering with UnionDocs for this screening, which represents the opening night of their two-week intensive workshop, “Wiseman’s New York”. Produced by UnionDocs and hosted by Genevieve Yue, this program is an in-depth exploration of Wiseman’s relationship to his most revisited location: New York City. Across 10 days, Yue will guide participants through a survey of Wiseman’s New York films, alongside visits to the institutions, neighborhoods, and civic spaces they document. Throughout the program, Yue is joined by filmmakers, critics, artists, and community members whose work is in conversation with Wiseman’s films, from a range of perspectives. Through screenings, discussions, site visits, and conversations, participants will consider how Wiseman’s extraordinary attention to place, labor, and public life continues to shape documentary practice today. For more info about UnionDocs’ workshop, “Wiseman’s New York”, visit: https://uniondocs.org/wisemans-new-york/

title: The Samurai and the Prisoner
description: Join us in the microcinema for Kiyoshi Kurosawa’s ponderous and philosophical samurai epic The Samurai and the Prisoner. When Lord Murashige rises up against the tyrannical Oda, he finds himself besieged within the walls of his own castle. Isolated, he is confronted with a series of mysterious crimes that shatter the fragile order of his court, plunging the fortress into fear and suspicion. With Oda’s army closing in and a traitor hiding among his ranks, Murashige is forced into an uneasy alliance with Kanbei, a brilliant and dangerous strategist held prisoner in the dungeon, as he must outwit his enemies and uncover the truth before time runs out.

title: PORTAL TO HELL
description: After a debt-collector finds a portal to hell in a washing machine at his local laundromat, he’s propositioned into feeding hell sinners to save his neighbor’s soul.

title: Once
description: Vidiots remembers the life and talent of the great musician and actor Glen Hansard with a special screening of the delightful musical romance Once .

title: The Women
description: Co-written by Anita Loos and Jane Murfin, The Women delivers 135 of them, each with a speaking role, to the exclusion of men. The delightfully witty and rapid-fire dialogue pours out of a cadre of familiar faces, including Norma Shearer, Joan Crawford, and Rosalind Russell. While most of the film unfolds in black-and-white, a delightful six-minute Technicolor fashion show is included, featuring gowns by Adrian, the iconic, MGM-based costume designer. Contributing to the distinctive looks of the cast was the uncredited hair designer, MGM veteran Sydney Guilaroff, whose film career spanned the 1930s to the 1980s and included such classics as Singin’ in the Rain (1952), North by Northwest (1959) and Who’s Afraid of Virginia Woolf? (1966)
director: George Cukor PRODUCED BY: Hunt Stromberg

title: Le Havre
description: Le Havre. 2011. Finland/France/Germany. Written and directed by Aki Kaurismäki. With André Wilms, Kati Outinen, Jean-Pierre Darroussin, Blondin Miguel. DCP. In French; English subtitles. 93 min. Inspired by French poetic realism of the 1930s, Aki Kaurismäki’s Le Havre takes us to the titular port city, where we meet Marcel Marx, an elderly shoeshiner and struggling writer named after a famous revolutionary socialist, and his wife Arletty, whose name pays tribute to the star of Marcel Carné’s Hôtel du Nord (1938), Le jour se lève (1939), and Les Enfants du Paradis (1945). When Marx crosses paths with an underage, undocumented immigrant hiding from police, the power of human solidarity, as often seen in Kaurismäki’s cinema, offers a glimmer of hope and a chance for resistance in a world that’s often too brutal to be reckoned with.

title: La Traviata on Sydney Harbour
description: La Traviata on Sydney Harbour Verdi’s hugely popular La Traviata returns to the Sydney Harbour water stage featuring a breath-taking soaring 9 metre high, 3.5 ton chandelier covered in 10,000 shimmering Swarovski crystals. This glamorous production was captured on location on Sydney Harbour in 2021 in front of a sold out audience. La Traviata features timeless romantic arias, lively choreography, beautiful costumes and spectacular fireworks.

title: Your Name.
description: One morning, rural schoolgirl Mitsuha and city kid Taki awaken to discover that they’ve switched bodies. The total strangers struggle to navigate each other’s lives, walking tightropes of intimacy and distance. But when they finally resolve to meet, the true nature of their connection threatens to seal their fate.

title: The Matrix
description: When a beautiful stranger leads computer hacker Neo to a forbidding underworld, he discovers the shocking truth--the life he knows is the elaborate deception of an evil cyber-intelligence.

title: ŞEYTAN
description:
A 12-year-old girl named Gül becomes possessed by Satan after experimenting with a Ouija board. As her condition worsens and medical explanations fail, her desperate mother turns to a psychiatrist and an experienced exorcist, who join forces in an attempt to save the girl through a dangerous ritual.
As an unofficial Turkish adaptation of The Exorcist, the film closely mirrors the broad structure of William Friedkin's original while relocating the story to contemporary Turkey. Despite its modest production, it has become a cult curiosity for its earnest reinterpretation of a landmark horror film within the context of 1970s Turkish genre cinema

title: Falling Down
description: A middle-aged man dealing with both unemployment and divorce, William Foster (Michael Douglas) is having a bad day. When his car breaks down on a Los Angeles highway, he leaves his vehicle and begins a trek across the city to attend his daughter's birthday party. As he makes his way through the urban landscape, William's frustration and bitterness become more evident, resulting in violent encounters with various people, including a vengeful gang and a dutiful veteran cop (Robert Duvall).

title: Monkey Business
description: Dr. Barnaby Fulton (Cary Grant) is a scatterbrained chemist working to create an elixir of youth. When one of his chimpanzees, Esther, breaks loose, she mixes chemicals in Barnaby’s lab, dumping the concoction into the office’s water cooler. The formula generates the rejuvenation effect Barnaby has been seeking — along with more chaotic side effects in some cases. Monkey Business allowed Monroe, who co-stars as Lois Laurel, to showcase her brilliant timing, further solidifying her reputation as a comedic actress.
director: Howard Hawks PRODUCED BY: Sol C. Siegel

title: The French Connection
description: New York Detective "Popeye" Doyle (Gene Hackman) and his partner (Roy Scheider) chase a French heroin smuggler.

title: Angel's Egg
description: In an underwater city, a young girl takes care of a large egg she holds carefully in her arms. A boy with a gun arrives in search of a bird he saw in his dream. At first, it seems as if feelings of sympathy are developing between the two. Forty years after the film’s original release, Anime Limited is proud to present an all-new 4K restoration of the film, supervised by director Mamoru Oshii, in cinemas nationwide for the very first time. The film is a creative collaboration between acclaimed director Mamoru Oshii (Ghost in the Shell), who wrote and directed the feature, and revered artist Yoshitaka Amano (Final Fantasy, Vampire Hunter D). The film beautifully intertwines Oshii’s thematic reflections on philosophy and theology with Amano’s distinctive ink painting style, culminating in an arrestingly beautiful hand-drawn allegorical fantasy.

title: Disintegration 93-96
description: Disintegration 93-96. 2017. USA. Directed by Miko Revereza. DCP. 5 min. No Data Plan. 2019. USA. Directed by Miko Revereza. DCP. 70 min. Manila-born Miko Revereza was an undocumented immigrant in the US for more than 20 years, an experience that fuels his artistic and personal exploration of diaspora and identity in a precarious, anti-migrant political environment. In his debut feature, No Data Plan, Revereza boards a New York–bound Amtrak train in Los Angeles, blending footage from his coast-to-coast trip with memories of faraway places and conversations with his mother amid a flight from immigration officers. In Disintegration 93-96, Revereza uses home-video footage from his childhood to look back on his move from the Philippines to California, offering a critical montage of the American dream and its reflections on one’s identity.

title: Hunt for the Wilderpeople (10th Anniversary)
description: Taika Waititi’s iconic film is back in 4K to celebrate its 10 year anniversary! Ricky (Julian Dennison) is a defiant young city kid who finds himself on the run with his grumpy foster uncle (Sam Neill). A national manhunt ensues and the two are forced to work together to survive.

title: Bitter Christmas (15) (AD)
description: Pedro Almodóvar is back with his unique brand of storytelling, setting the stage for the tale of a filmmaker who is a little too heavily inspired by the real lives of those around him.

title: I Want Your Sex
description: Gregg Araki's I Want Your Sex tells the story of Elliot (Cooper Hoffman), a kind-hearted if unmotivated twentysomething whose fantasies quickly come true when he lands a job with renowned artist and provocateur Erika Tracy (Olivia Wilde). When Erika breaks down office boundaries and takes Elliot on as her sexual muse and subordinate, their sexually charged relationship makes him question his own desires, boundaries, and relationships with his uptight girlfriend (Charli XCX) and repressed roommate (Chase Sui Wonders). As the stakes heighten and power dynamics shift, the film mixes satire, romantic comedy, mystery, and murder through the colourful and edgy visual language for which Araki is best known.

title: Kino Polonia: IDA
description: Kino Polonia presents  IDA  dir. Pawel Pawlikowski | PL/DK | 2013  Poland, 1962. Anna, a novice nun preparing to take her vows, discovers a family secret that changes her understanding of her past. Together with her aunt, she embarks on a journey to uncover the fate of her family during and after th...

title: RED SPIRIT LAKE
description:
A young woman inherits a secluded house beside Red Spirit Lake after the murder of a relative. When her friends arrive to help her settle in, their stay is interrupted by a series of brutal killings carried out by a group of violent locals, forcing the survivors into a desperate struggle to uncover the secrets surrounding the lake and stay alive.
Blending backwoods slasher conventions with no-budget underground filmmaking, the film mixes graphic violence, occult overtones, and abrasive punk aesthetics into an intentionally raw and confrontational horror experience. Its fragmented structure and DIY style have made it a cult title within American underground cinema.

title: I WANT YOUR SEX
description: A bold, provocative, and wickedly funny erotic comedy-thriller from cult filmmaker Gregg Araki (Mysterious Skin, The Doom Generation). Olivia Wilde and Cooper Hoffman lead an irresistible ensemble cast featuring Charli XCX, Chase Sui Wonders, Mason Gooding and Daveed Diggs. Following its buzzy Sunda...

title: Barry Lyndon
description: Stanley Kubrick’s follow-up to the foreboding A Clockwork Orange (1971) is a stately, gorgeously crafted, epic adaptation of William Makepeace Thackeray’s novel about the curious fates of an Irish rogue. Ryan O’Neal portrays Lyndon, and the film earned seven nominations, including Best Picture, Directing, and Adapted Screenplay (all for Kubrick), with Oscars going to the Art Direction, Costume Design, Adaptation Score, and John Alcott’s painterly, natural and candlelit cinematography, which remains immensely influential.

title: WRITTEN ON THE WIND
description: Alcoholism, nymphomania, impotence, and deadly jealousy fill the screen in Douglas Sirk’s Technicolor operatic tragedy, WRITTEN ON THE WIND. Mitch Wayne, played by Rock Hudson, works hard as a geologist for the Texan oil-rich degenerate Hadleys who envelope him in their maelstrom of psychosexual angst and fury.

title: First Cow
description: First Cow. 2019. USA. Directed by Kelly Reichardt. Screenplay by Reichardt, Jonathan Raymond, based on Raymond’s book. With John Magaro, Orion Lee, Toby Jones, Ewen Bremner, Scott Shepherd, Gary Farmer, Lily Gladstone. DCP. 121 min. In early-19th-century Oregon Territory, Cookie (John Magaro), a sensitive outsider in debt to brutish fur traders, and King Lu (Orion Lee), an affable, philosophizing Chinese immigrant, form a tender brotherhood amid rough surroundings. The two dream of a better future—and find a way to finance one with the arrival of the territory’s first cow, whose milk they surreptitiously turn into sweet treats to sell. Though cinematographer Christopher Blauvelt cocoons the viewer in verdant nature, moonlight, and the warmth of human connection, the very real terrors of capitalism and colonialism are never too far out of frame. In her seventh feature, Kelly Reichardt masterfully weaves these complex themes together, creating an intimate glimpse of the grand tragedy and beauty of the American experiment.

title: Speed Racer
description: Speed Racer is a young and brilliant racing driver. When corruption in the racing leagues costs his brother his life, Speed must team up with the police and the mysterious Racer X to bring an end to the corruption and criminal activities.

title: Yojimbo
description: Eternal icon Toshirō Mifune stars in this darkly comic and visually arresting masterpiece from the inimitable Akira Kurosawa. To rid a terror-stricken village of corruption, the wise ronin Sanjuro pits two evil clans against each other to his own advantage. Remade twice officially (which included a plagiarism lawsuit filed against Sergio Leone) with ripples of influence throughout the Western genre in both America and Italy, this exhilarating genre-twister remains one of the most influential and entertaining films of all time. Don’t miss all the samurai action you can handle on the big screen!

title: CITY LIGHTS
description: CITY LIGHTS, the most cherished film by Charlie Chaplin, is also his ultimate Little Tramp chronicle. The writer-director-star achieved new levels of grace, in both physical comedy and dramatic poignancy, with this silent tale of a lovable vagrant falling for a young blind woman who sells flowers on the street (a magical Virginia Cherrill) and mistakes him for a millionaire. Though this Depression-era smash was made after the advent of sound, Chaplin remained steadfast in his love for the expressive beauty of the pre-talkie form. The result was the epitome of his art and the crowning achievement of silent comedy.

title: MIX NYC PRESENTS: EARLY INTERIORITY: VINTAGE TRANS CINEMA
description: This program gathers rare vintage short films that open a portal to trans feminine interior life between 1967 and 1982. We meet these women in moments of quiet confidence, everyday mundanity, and enduring glamour. Through deeply intimate portraits, these films unearth buried pieces of trans history while illuminating how the world has long constricted trans women’s freedom to be. Made under a police state, these portraits mirror the experiences of trans femmes today. Each woman captured becomes a living testament to ancestral resilience and the enduring necessity of trans documentation. This program is co-curated by Thee Rose and Rosalina Michele for MIX NYC, one of the oldest queer experimental film festivals in the world. Special thanks to the Institute for Studies on Latin American Art (ISLAA); to Bradford Nordeen for providing the digital exhibition files; and to the Film-Makers' Coop for providing the 16mm prints. Nikolai Ursin BEHIND EVERY GOOD MAN (1967, 8 min, 16mm) Marguerite Paris ALL WOMEN ARE EQUAL (1972, 15 min, 16mm. Preserved by MIX NYC and the Women’s Film Preservation Fund via New York Women in Film & Television.) Joseph Horning VALERIE (1975, 16 min, 16mm-to-DCP) Manuel Herreros de Lemos & Mateo Manaure Arilla TRANS (1982, 22 min, 16mm-to-DCP) Total running time: ca. 65 min. Followed by a discussion between curators Thee Rose and Rosalina Michele, moderated by Kristen Lovell (co-director of THE STROLL).

title: Pink Palace: Fassbinder – Fox and His Friends
description: Pink Palace presents this gritty look at the seduction of a working class gay man by the bourgeois materialistic middle classes of 1970’s West Germany.  Fox and His Friends is among the director’s most personal works and the first to tackle homosexuality in a direct manner. Fassbinder himself plays ...

title: TWISTED ISSUES
description:
A teenage skateboarder is murdered by a gang of local punks, only to return from the grave on his skateboard to exact revenge on those responsible. As his killing spree unfolds, the story collides with live punk performances, skate culture, surreal comedy, and bursts of graphic gore, creating an increasingly chaotic portrait of late-1980s underground youth culture.
Rather than following a conventional slasher structure, the film functions as a DIY snapshot of the Gainesville, Florida punk scene, mixing horror, music, satire, and experimental collage. Its anarchic editing, homemade effects, and regional soundtrack give it the feel of a time capsule as much as a revenge film.

title: DER FAN
description: Simone (the magnetic Désirée Nosbusch) is a teenage runaway who is obsessed with the pop singer known as “R.” Soon, that obsession takes over her life. When “R” uses Simone with machine-like coldness, she plots her revenge with an unholy ceremony that’s equally romantic and horrifying. Fueled by a killer minimalist synth soundtrack from Rheingold and a gorgeous design aesthetic, DER FAN is a subversive and electric shocker that goes harder than you’d ever expect it to go.

title: The Invite             / Bob & Carol & Ted & Alice
description: Joe and Angela’s marriage is on thin ice. When they invite their enigmatic upstairs neighbors for a dinner party, the night spirals into unexpected places. Have they reignited the spark or lit the match that burns it all down? (A24)

title: La Haine
description: Hatred breeds hatred... 24 hours in the lives of three young men in the French suburbs the day after a violent riot.

title: The Terminator
description: Disguised as a human, a cyborg assassin known as a Terminator (Arnold Schwarzenegger) travels from 2029 to 1984 to kill Sarah Connor (Linda Hamilton). Sent to protect Sarah is Kyle Reese (Michael Biehn), who divulges the coming of Skynet, an artificial intelligence system that will spark a nuclear holocaust. Sarah is targeted because Skynet knows that her unborn son will lead the fight against them. With the virtually unstoppable Terminator in hot pursuit, she and Kyle attempt to escape. 40th Anniversary restoration from a 4K film scan of the 35mm negative and a new Dolby Atmos mix with final sound and picture approved by director James Cameron. Presented by Park Circus with thanks to MGM. Post House: Park Road Post, Colourist: Tashi Trieu, Sound Mixer for Atmos: Mike Hedges

title: Onslaught
description: When a rogue squad of genetically engineered super soldiers break loose in the desert, a badass Army sniper must unleash hell to protect her young daughter.

title: CLEAN, SHAVEN
description: Lodge Kerrigan began his succession of utterly unique, visually and aurally dazzling character studies with the raw, ravaging CLEAN, SHAVEN. A compelling headfirst dive into the mindscape of a schizophrenic (played by the remarkable Peter Greene) as he tries to track down his daughter after he is released from an institution, Kerrigan’s film brilliantly uses sound and image to lead audiences into a terrifying subjectivity. No one is left unscathed.

title: Trainspotting
description: Choose life. Choose a job. Choose a starter home. Choose dental insurance, leisure wear and matching luggage. Choose your future. But why would anyone want to do a thing like that? Director Danny Boyle’s electrifying look at the exhilarating highs and terrifying lows of the Edinburgh drug scene is daringly original, energetically stylish, and brutally funny, with a stellar ensemble including Ewan McGregor, Jonny Lee Miller, and Robert Carlyle, plus one of the most iconic soundtracks of the ‘90s.

title: In The Mood For Love
description: In 1962 Hong Kong, neighbors Su Li-zhen (Mrs. Chan) and Chow Mo-wan (Mr. Chow) discover their spouses are having an affair. As they spend time together, they develop feelings for each other, but their relationship remains chaste and unspoken, reflecting societal constraints and their own moral compass.

title: Terminator 2 : Judgment Day
description: In this sequel set eleven years after "The Terminator," young John Connor (Edward Furlong), the key to civilization's victory over a future robot uprising, is the target of the shape-shifting T-1000 (Robert Patrick), a Terminator sent from the future to kill him. Another Terminator, the revamped T-800 (Arnold Schwarzenegger), has been sent back to protect the boy. As John and his mother (Linda Hamilton) go on the run with the T-800, the boy forms an unexpected bond with the robot.

title: The Samurai and the Prisoner
description: Join us in the microcinema for Kiyoshi Kurosawa’s ponderous and philosophical samurai epic The Samurai and the Prisoner. When Lord Murashige rises up against the tyrannical Oda, he finds himself besieged within the walls of his own castle. Isolated, he is confronted with a series of mysterious crimes that shatter the fragile order of his court, plunging the fortress into fear and suspicion. With Oda’s army closing in and a traitor hiding among his ranks, Murashige is forced into an uneasy alliance with Kanbei, a brilliant and dangerous strategist held prisoner in the dungeon, as he must outwit his enemies and uncover the truth before time runs out.

title: Onslaught
description: When a rogue squad of genetically engineered super soldiers break loose in the desert, a badass Army sniper must unleash hell to protect her young daughter.

title: UNION COUNTY
description: Will Poulter and Noah Centineo deliver pitch-perfect performances as brothers Cody and Jack Parsons, each navigating a court-mandated drug rehabilitation program in a pocket of rural Ohio hit hard by the opioid epidemic. Provided with hope for the first time since their struggles began and with the support of a tireless counselor (Annette Deao), the brothers work toward a brighter, sober future.

title: Le Havre
description: Le Havre. 2011. Finland/France/Germany. Written and directed by Aki Kaurismäki. With André Wilms, Kati Outinen, Jean-Pierre Darroussin, Blondin Miguel. DCP. In French; English subtitles. 93 min. Inspired by French poetic realism of the 1930s, Aki Kaurismäki’s Le Havre takes us to the titular port city, where we meet Marcel Marx, an elderly shoeshiner and struggling writer named after a famous revolutionary socialist, and his wife Arletty, whose name pays tribute to the star of Marcel Carné’s Hôtel du Nord (1938), Le jour se lève (1939), and Les Enfants du Paradis (1945). When Marx crosses paths with an underage, undocumented immigrant hiding from police, the power of human solidarity, as often seen in Kaurismäki’s cinema, offers a glimmer of hope and a chance for resistance in a world that’s often too brutal to be reckoned with.

title: Leviticus
description: Two teenage boys must escape a violent entity that takes the form of the person they desire most - each other.…

Late Fame
description: Willem Defoe plays Ed Saxberger, a forgotten New York poet, who works in the post office. After an eager and flattering young admirer appears on his doorstep, Saxberger is beckoned into a coterie of twentysomething admirers who anoint him as a rediscovered genius. Intoxicated by the attention — and by the alluring presence of Gloria, the group’s “tragic heroine” — Saxberger gradually reckons with the authenticity of his newfound poetic circle. Kent Jones's thoughtful, witty film is a wistful yet unromantic look at a lost idea of downtown New York.

title: ELEVATOR GIRLS IN BONDAGE + MYSTERY SHORT
description:
The underpaid female staff of a rundown San Francisco hotel discover the writings of Karl Marx and begin organising a revolt against their exploitative employers. Led by elevator operator Maxine, the workers fight back against low wages, poor conditions, and the abusive behaviour of the hotel’s management in this anarchic underground comedy.
Created by members of the legendary San Francisco drag and performance collective The Cockettes, Michael Kalmen’s film is a surreal mixture of camp, queer underground cinema, political satire, and sexploitation. Its deliberately chaotic style, gender-bending performances, and Marxist-inspired rebellion make it a unique artefact of the early 1970s counterculture scene.
Preceded by an outrageous 30 minute shot-on-video bizarro sci-fi fetish film...

title: WHAT GODMILOW TAUGHT
description: FILMMAKER IN PERSON! In 2012, Jill Godmilow wrote to Mireia Sallarès, moved by the film she had made in Mexico about women’s orgasms. For Godmilow, who offered to help distribute the film in the U.S., LAS MUERTES CHIQUITAS (THE LITTLE DEATHS) is not a documentary about a problem of Mexican women, it is a film about orgasms as a political issue that affects everyone and raises the question of who can take responsibility for it by speaking out. How to take responsibility for our problems, how to take charge of them by making political films, was the concern that had led Godmilow to engage years earlier with Harun Farocki’s documentary INEXTINGUISHABLE FIRE, which showed how napalm production during the Vietnam War effectively exempted its makers from any responsibility for it. The fact that Farocki’s film had not been seen in the U.S. and that the problem it raised had not gone away, Godmilow decided to recreate it, in order to involve herself in the problem and put it back into circulation. As a statement about what it means today to be an author, and taking account of this complexity by broadening and politicizing the chain of authorship, she titled her replica WHAT FAROCKI TAUGHT. The present film, WHAT GODMILOW TAUGHT (2014), is a film conversation in which Mireia Sallarès captures Jill Godmilow’s commitment to a political life. Sallarès’s film engages with an artistic practice in which having an idea entails a responsibility, and in which grappling with a political problem requires collaborating with others to make useful films. Followed by: Jill Godmilow ECSTATIC ORGASM 7.5-min excerpt from an unfinished film, digital Total running time: ca. 60 min.

title: HUNT FOR THE WILDERPEOPLE
description: Nature just got gangster! Young actor Julian Dennison gives a masterful Oscar-worthy performance in Taika Waititi’s hilarious and enormously entertaining magical-realism backwoods saga HUNT FOR THE WILDERPEOPLE. Raised on hip-hop and foster care, defiant delinquent Ricky (Dennison) gets a fresh start in the New Zealand countryside with the loving Aunt Bella, the ornery Uncle Hec and dog Tupac. When a tragedy strikes that threatens to ship Ricky to another home, both he and Hec go on the run in the bush. Upon a national manhunt, the outlaws must face their options: go out in a blaze of glory or overcome their differences and survive as a family. Triumphant, touching, surreal and just about perfect.

title: Mutts
description: Mutts. 2019. Canada. Directed by Halima Ouardiri. DCP. 18 min. Man Push Cart. 2005. USA. Written and directed by Ramin Bahrani. With Ahmad Razvi, Leticia Dolera, Charles Daniel Sandoval. 35mm. 87 min. Inspired by lead actor Ahmad Razvi’s life story, Ramin Bahrani’s Man Push Cart offers a melancholic look at post-9/11 New York from the perspective of a Pakistani immigrant—a former rock star in his native country, now a widower estranged from his son in Pakistan—as he struggles to make a living selling coffee and bagels, dragging a heavy cart through the cold, impersonal streets of Midtown Manhattan. Two decades later, Bahrani’s celebrated debut film remains a subtle look at the lives of those pushed to the margins of the American dream in a city marked by a lack of human connection. In Mutts, Halima Ouardiri films a large sanctuary in Morocco, filled with hundreds of stray dogs, and uses it as a metaphor for the struggles of refugees and life in poverty and confinement.

description: The latest production from boundlessly imaginative Argentine collective El Pampero Cine sees successive pairs of characters bid farewell: a mother and her son, a caretaker and her charge, two actors endlessly rehearsing a scene that will never be performed. A playful spin on theatrical adaptation, Alejo Moguillansky's new film is a delightfully imaginative take on Samuel Beckett's Fin de Partie , punctuated by music, tennis, and another exceptional turn by Laura Paredes. The UK Premiere screening on the 4 September will be followed by an in-person Q&A with Alejo Moguillansky.

description: Two teenage boys must escape a violent entity that takes the form of the person they desire most - each other.…

title: Romeo + Juliet
description: Baz Luhrmann’s take on Shakespeare’s tragedy is perhaps one of the best-loved adaptations and is the second installment in his Red Curtain Trilogy, which closed with Moulin Rouge! (2001). Featuring Luhrmann’s distinctive, stylized palate coupled with frenetic, MTV-style editing and an all-star soundtrack, Romeo + Juliet became a classic for its casting, with Leonardo DiCaprio and Claire Danes playing the star-crossed lovers.

title: WHEN HARRY MET SALLY
description: Harry (Billy Crystal) and Sally (Meg Ryan) meet in college and spend years debating whether it’s possible for men and women to be friends – all the while falling in love without realizing it. Nora Ephron’s landmark screenplay is filled with quotable lines and sharp insights, and costars Bruno Kirby and Carrie Fisher lend hilarious support. One of the definitive romantic comedies of the ’80s.

title: WHAT FAROCKI TAUGHT + SCUM MANIFESTO
description: Jill Godmilow WHAT FAROCKI TAUGHT 1997, 30 min, 16mm. Made in collaboration with Gloria Jean Masciarotte & Ted Mandell. WHAT FAROCKI TAUGHT is literally and stubbornly a remake – that is, a perfect replica in color and in English, of Harun Farocki’s black-and-white, 1969 German language film, INEXTINGUISHABLE FIRE. Taking as its subject the political and formal strategies of Farocki’s film about the development of Napalm B by Dow Chemical during the Vietnam War, Godmilow’s unabashedly perfect copy reopens Walter Benjamin’s discussion of art in the age of mechanical reproduction. WHAT FAROCKI TAUGHT thus becomes an agit-prop challenge to the cinéma vérité documentary’s representation of information, history, politics, and “real” human experience. Because Farocki’s film was not in distribution in the U.S. at the time, WHAT FAROCKI TAUGHT was conceived as a gesture of film distribution – taking this small, film footnote to a war, a barnacle stuck on the side of the moth-balled vessel of Vietnam, flicking it forward past the recent, more sophisticated, and successful technologies of Panama and the Persian Gulf, to see if the “ping” of recognition and the radical potential of the documentary film project could be revived. Jill Godmilow SCUM MANIFESTO 2016, 27 min, digital. Made in collaboration with Joanna Krakowska & Magda Mosiewicz. When Sherry Millner and Ernest Larsen, the producers of the Facets DVD compilation “Disruptive Film”, couldn’t clear the rights to Delphine Seyrig and Carole Roussopoulos’s 1976 French film, SCUM MANIFESTO, they contacted Jill Godmilow, Queen of Replicas (see WHAT FAROCKI TAUGHT), who decided to produce a perfect Polish copy of this landmark film about the 1967 feminist manifesto – this time with Polish performers and current Polish newsreel of goings-on in the newly super-nationalist Polish state. Exactly as in the 1976 French film, the Poles translate then type up, phrase-by-phrase, Valerie Solanas’s still outrageous and profoundly useful 1967 text, which begins, “Life in this society being, at best, an utter bore and no aspect of society being at all relevant to women, there remains to civic-minded, responsible, thrill-seeking females only to overthrow the government, eliminate the money system, institute complete automation and destroy the male sex.” Total running time: ca. 60 min.

title: MYSTERY EROTIC THRILLER
description:
Mystery Erotic Thriller presents undisclosed deep cuts from the genre’s overheated history - from neon-soaked 80s neo-noir and glossy 90s studio sleaze to forgotten direct-to-video delirium. Expect dangerous affairs, obsessive desire, double-crosses, voyeurism, murder and exquisitely bad decisions, as sex becomes a weapon and nobody proves quite as innocent as they first appear. Come blind, surrender to the mystery and discover a film you may never otherwise have thought to see.
These screenings are strictly for adult audiences and may contain explicit sexual content, violence and other potentially offensive material. Do not attend if you are of a sensitive disposition. Adults only.

description: A mysterious Hollywood action film stuntman gets in trouble with gangsters when he tries to help his neighbor’s husband rob a pawn shop while serving as his getaway driver.

title: The Holy Mountain
description: Pack your bags for the head-trip of a lifetime with Alejandro Jodorowsky’s dazzling masterpiece and one of the most mind-bending feature films of all time. The Alchemist assembles together a group of people from all walks of life to represent the planets in the solar system. The occult adept’s intention is to put his recruits through strange mystical rites and divest them of their worldly baggage before embarking on a trip to Lotus Island. There they ascend the Holy Mountain to displace the immortal gods who secretly rule the universe. You’ll want to hold onto your eyeballs as you witness this psychedelic treasure on the big screen!

title: GYPSY 83
description: Sandusky, Ohio is hell on earth for goth misfits and Stevie Nicks superfans Gypsy Vale (Sara Rue) and her younger, queer protégée Clive Webb (Birkett Turton). When they discover a New York City club is hosting a “Night of 1000 Stevies,” the pair hit the road with high hopes that Gypsy will be able to perform. Along the way, they encounter other misfits who pave the way to their salvation, all while discovering profound truths about themselves. Costarring John Doe of the legendary punk band X and the great Karen Black as a has-been lounge singer, Todd Stephens’s cult favorite puts a queer, outsider spin on both the road movie and the coming-of-age journey, with plenty of black eyeliner to spare.

title: CatVideoFest 2026
description: Our fuzzy overlords return to the big screen! Vidiots is purrfectly enthralled to bring back the cutest kitty compilation ever! CatVideoFest is a compilation reel of the latest and best cat videos culled from countless hours of unique submissions and sourced animations, music videos, and classic internet powerhouses. CatVideoFest is a joyous communal experience, only available in theaters, and raises money for cats in need through partnerships with local cat charities, animal welfare organizations, and shelters to best serve cats in the area.

title: Kill Bill: Volume 1
description: Her child is gone. Her team of assassins has betrayed her. Now snatch your Pussy Wagon keychains off the hook and join us as Uma Thurman’s The Bride sets out in her search of vengeance to Kill Bill .

title: The Maltese Falcon             / The Petrified Forest
description: Everyone’s looking for it and they’ll do anything to get it! The Maltese Falcon , that is. It’s not just the opulent treasure in the mind’s eye of every San Francisco low-life, it’s also one of the first shining examples of Hollywood noir, a stunningly confident directing debut for John Huston, and a sordid melodrama which transformed Humphrey Bogart from B-movie sideman to star romantic lead. Mary Astor co-stars as the hot-blooded but inscrutable femme fatale who drags hard-boiled private eye Sam Spade (Bogart) into the hunt for the Falcon. Peter Lorre and Sydney Greenstreet (in his Academy Award-nominated film debut!) round out the conspiratorial cast as dandy-gangsters with twisted loyalties. The paradigm for film noir to come, this loaded, sordid mystery gets right to the tragic truth about love and crime: “It’s the stuff that dreams are made of.”

title: Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs
description: Snow White, orphaned as a child, is forced to work under the reign of her evil stepmother, the Queen, who will stop at nothing to remain the most beautiful being in the land. When Snow White’s beauty grows, so does the Queen’s jealously. Seething with hatred, the Queen concocts a sinister plan to put an end to her. Will the princess escape her fate and achieve her happily ever after? Based on the classic Brothers Grimm fairy tale, this first animated feature from The Walt Disney Company—and the first traditionally animated feature ever produced— was nominated for its original score; the following year, the Academy gave Disney a Special Award for the film (one full-sized Oscar and seven small ones), “recognized as a significant screen innovation which has charmed millions and pioneered a great new entertainment field for the motion picture cartoon.”
director: David Hand, Perce Pearce, William Cottrell, Larry Morey, Wilfred Jackson, Ben Sharpsteen PRODUCED BY: Walt Disney

title: Rio
description: This comedy-adventure centers on Blu, a flightless rare macaw who acts more human than bird. His world is turned upside down…

title: Moana Sing-Along
description: Sing along with this modern animated classic of a powerful girl pursuing her destiny and identity! Moana is on a daring mission to save her people, sailing out in the seas of the mighty Pacific with determination. Along the way she meets the once-mighty demigod Maui, who guides her towards her goal of becoming a master way-finder. Together they sail across the open ocean on an action-packed voyage, encountering enormous monsters and impossible odds. Along the way, Moana fulfills the ancient quest of her ancestors and discovers the one thing she always sought: her own identity. With a fun and inspiring soundtrack that includes tracks by Lin-Manuel Miranda, here’s your chance to belt out your favorite tunes with folks who love it as much as you do!

title: UNTIL THE END OF THE WORLD
description: In order to enable his blind wife (Jeanne Moreau) to see, Dr. Farber (Max von Sydow) invents a process that makes it possible to transmit the images recorded in the brains of sighted people directly into the visual systems of blind people. Farber’s son Sam (William Hurt) sets out on a journey around the world in order to “see” and record the various stations of his mother’s life for her. The Frenchwoman Claire (Solveig Dommartin) falls in love with him and sets out in pursuit of him. She, in turn, is followed by the author Eugene (Sam Neill), who is recording her adventure.

description: Alcoholism, nymphomania, impotence, and deadly jealousy fill the screen in Douglas Sirk’s Technicolor operatic tragedy, WRITTEN ON THE WIND. Mitch Wayne, played by Rock Hudson, works hard as a geologist for the Texan oil-rich degenerate Hadleys who envelope him in their maelstrom of psychosexual angst and fury.

title: Pee-wee’s Big Adventure
description: The story of a rebel and his bike. In Tim Burton’s dynamite feature length directorial debut, Pee-wee Herman explodes to life in one of the most exciting, creatively colorful, constantly quotable and enduring comedies of the decade! When his fully customized, fire engine red bicycle is stolen, Pee-wee sets off on a Big Adventure to get it back, hitchhiking cross-country and encountering a quirky cast of new friends along the way.

title: Fanny & Alexander
description: Swedish auteur Ingmar Bergman’s most sentimental and autobiographical work is set in turn-of-the-century Sweden and appropriately bathed in the candlelit interiors common of the era. Unfolding through the eyes of 10-year-old Alexander, a boy from a wealthy family that operates the town theater, the narrative spans seasons and holidays, marriages and deaths, with small moments of daily life punctuating childhood milestones. Originally conceived as a television miniseries of more than five hours, the final, 188-minute version allowed the visuals of two-time Oscar-winning cinematographer Sven Nykvist ( Fanny & Alexander was one of his wins) to be admired at a scale befitting this epic drama.

title: The Samurai and the Prisoner
description: Join us in the microcinema for Kiyoshi Kurosawa’s ponderous and philosophical samurai epic The Samurai and the Prisoner. When Lord Murashige rises up against the tyrannical Oda, he finds himself besieged within the walls of his own castle. Isolated, he is confronted with a series of mysterious crimes that shatter the fragile order of his court, plunging the fortress into fear and suspicion. With Oda’s army closing in and a traitor hiding among his ranks, Murashige is forced into an uneasy alliance with Kanbei, a brilliant and dangerous strategist held prisoner in the dungeon, as he must outwit his enemies and uncover the truth before time runs out.

description: I have been and always shall be your friend. Beam yourself up to the Starship Enterprise for a double shot of intergalactic fun and twice the Ricardo Montalban with one of the best films in the franchise, and an all-time classic of Science Fiction cinema Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan plus a bonus episode of the original series that inspired the film: Space Seed . Spock, Kirk, and the stalwart crew of the iconic Starship Enterprise are pulled back into action when old nemesis, the menacing villain Khan, steals a top-secret device called Project Genesis. Now the Enterprise is heading towards an intergalactic showdown in space! We’re setting our lasers (and projector) to stun!

title: SAMBA TRAORÉ
description: The only surviving accomplice of a gas station robbery gone bad, Samba Traoré flees the scene of the crime with a suitcase full of cash for his native village in rural Burkina Faso. There he attempts to make a fresh start while hiding how he came by his new fortune from those around him. Despite marrying the beautiful Saratou, earning the affection of her ten-year-old son, and opening a bar with his childhood friend, Samba’s newfound happiness is put to the test as he struggles to cope with the moral crisis of his crimes.

title: First Cow
description: First Cow. 2019. USA. Directed by Kelly Reichardt. Screenplay by Reichardt, Jonathan Raymond, based on Raymond’s book. With John Magaro, Orion Lee, Toby Jones, Ewen Bremner, Scott Shepherd, Gary Farmer, Lily Gladstone. DCP. 121 min. In early-19th-century Oregon Territory, Cookie (John Magaro), a sensitive outsider in debt to brutish fur traders, and King Lu (Orion Lee), an affable, philosophizing Chinese immigrant, form a tender brotherhood amid rough surroundings. The two dream of a better future—and find a way to finance one with the arrival of the territory’s first cow, whose milk they surreptitiously turn into sweet treats to sell. Though cinematographer Christopher Blauvelt cocoons the viewer in verdant nature, moonlight, and the warmth of human connection, the very real terrors of capitalism and colonialism are never too far out of frame. In her seventh feature, Kelly Reichardt masterfully weaves these complex themes together, creating an intimate glimpse of the grand tragedy and beauty of the American experiment.

title: WISE BLOOD
description:
Returning from military service to a transformed American South, Hazel Motes arrives in a small Georgia city determined to reject the religious convictions that shaped his childhood. Proclaiming himself the founder of the "Church Without Christ", he embarks on a furious campaign against belief, attracting a succession of eccentric followers, opportunists, and would-be prophets. As Hazel's crusade against faith grows increasingly obsessive, his attempts to escape spiritual certainty lead him toward acts of self-destruction that mirror the fervour he claims to oppose.
Adapted from Flannery O'Connor's 1952 novel, Wise Blood occupies a distinctive place within John Huston's later work, combining Southern Gothic, black comedy, and religious allegory. Filmed in Georgia near O'Connor's home territory and closely preserving the novel's dialogue and structure, the film translates her world of preachers, charlatans, and spiritual seekers into a landscape where belief and disbelief become equally consuming forces. Anchored by Brad Dourif's remarkable performance, Wise Blood explores evangelical culture, American individualism, and the uneasy relationship between modernity and faith, resulting in one of the most unusual literary adaptations of the 1970s.
Introduced by regular programmer and filmmaker Craig Williams

The total strangers struggle to navigate each other’s lives, walking tightropes of intimacy and distance. But when they finally resolve to meet, the true nature of their connection threatens to seal their fate.

title: WHAT GODMILOW TAUGHT
description: FILMMAKER IN PERSON! In 2012, Jill Godmilow wrote to Mireia Sallarès, moved by the film she had made in Mexico about women’s orgasms. For Godmilow, who offered to help distribute the film in the U.S., LAS MUERTES CHIQUITAS (THE LITTLE DEATHS) is not a documentary about a problem of Mexican women, it is a film about orgasms as a political issue that affects everyone and raises the question of who can take responsibility for it by speaking out. How to take responsibility for our problems, how to take charge of them by making political films, was the concern that had led Godmilow to engage years earlier with Harun Farocki’s documentary INEXTINGUISHABLE FIRE, which showed how napalm production during the Vietnam War effectively exempted its makers from any responsibility for it. The fact that Farocki’s film had not been seen in the U.S. and that the problem it raised had not gone away, Godmilow decided to recreate it, in order to involve herself in the problem and put it back into circulation. As a statement about what it means today to be an author, and taking account of this complexity by broadening and politicizing the chain of authorship, she titled her replica WHAT FAROCKI TAUGHT. The present film, WHAT GODMILOW TAUGHT (2014), is a film conversation in which Mireia Sallarès captures Jill Godmilow’s commitment to a political life. Sallarès’s film engages with an artistic practice in which having an idea entails a responsibility, and in which grappling with a political problem requires collaborating with others to make useful films. Followed by: Jill Godmilow ECSTATIC ORGASM 7.5-min excerpt from an unfinished film, digital Total running time: ca. 60 min.

title: Late Fame
description: Willem Defoe plays Ed Saxberger, a forgotten New York poet, who works in the post office. After an eager and flattering young admirer appears on his doorstep, Saxberger is beckoned into a coterie of twentysomething admirers who anoint him as a rediscovered genius. Intoxicated by the attention — and by the alluring presence of Gloria, the group’s “tragic heroine” — Saxberger gradually reckons with the authenticity of his newfound poetic circle. Kent Jones's thoughtful, witty film is a wistful yet unromantic look at a lost idea of downtown New York.

title: JUBILEE
description:
After an encounter with the occult philosopher John Dee, Queen Elizabeth I is transported from the sixteenth century into a near-future Britain marked by social collapse, media saturation, and authoritarian control. Arriving in a London populated by punk gangs, aspiring pop stars, political extremists, and cultural opportunists, she witnesses a society in which traditional institutions have disintegrated and power has been absorbed by entertainment, violence, and spectacle. Moving between squats, wastelands, recording studios, and ruined urban spaces, the film unfolds as a series of encounters rather than a conventional narrative.
Widely regarded as the first British punk film, Jubilee emerged directly from the cultural ferment of late-1970s London and features appearances from figures associated with the punk and post-punk scene, including Toyah Willcox, Jordan, Adam Ant, and Gene October. Rather than functioning as a celebration of punk culture, Derek Jarman's film subjects both the establishment and the counterculture to sustained scrutiny, presenting a vision of Britain shaped by commodification, nationalism, and social decay. Combining historical fantasy, political satire, and experimental filmmaking, Jubilee remains one of the key cinematic responses to the economic and cultural crises that transformed Britain during the 1970s.

title: Tremors
description: There’s something under the ground! An isolated town is on the menu for the giant, subterranean Graboids and it is up to Kevin Bacon, Fred Ward, Michael Gross, and Reba McEntire to get everyone out alive! With some of the best monster effects of the entire 1990s on full display in the desert sun, this cult-classic delivers the scares, thrills, and laughs of a creature feature that is truly Perfection.

title: I VITELLONI
description: Five young men linger in a postadolescent limbo, dreaming of adventure and escape from their small seacoast town. They while away their time spending the lira doled out by their indulgent families on drink, women and nights at the local pool hall. Federico Fellini’s second solo directorial effort is a semiautobiographical masterpiece of sharply drawn character sketches: Skirt chaser Fausto, forced to marry a girl he has impregnated; Alberto, the perpetual child; Leopoldo, a writer thirsting for fame; and Moraldo, the only member of the group troubled by a moral conscience. An international success and recipient of an Academy Award nomination for Best Original Screenplay, I VITELLONI compassionately details a year in the life of a group of small-town layabouts struggling to find meaning in their lives.

title: "There They Go-Go-Go!" / A FEW GOOD MEN
description: Wile E. Coyote is so hungry that he forms a chicken out of mud, bakes it and tries to eat it, causing one of his teeth to fall out. He throws the mud bird away when a real one comes along – the Road Runner, who runs so fast that he literally burns up the road, setting Wile E.’s feet on fire!

title: Lingua Franca
description: Lingua Franca. 2019. USA/Philippines. Written and directed by Isabel Sandoval. With Sandoval, Eamon Farren, Ivory Aquino, P.J. Boudousqué, Lev Gorn, Lynn Cohen. DCP. In English, Cebuano, Filipino, Russian. 84 min. In her third feature film (and her first primarily in English), actor-director Isabel Sandoval plays Olivia, an undocumented Filipina trans woman who works as a caregiver for Olga, an elderly Russian Jewish woman with early dementia living in New York’s Brighton Beach. Fearing capture and deportation by ICE, Olivia splits her meager earnings between her family in the Philippines and an American-born man with whom she hopes to secure permanent residency through a marriage of convenience. When she crosses paths with Alex, Olga’s grandson, after he returns home from mandated rehab in Russia, her plans—and future—are upended by the power of affection and the hidden pains of displacement.

title: ROY COHN/JACK SMITH
description: From one of the seminal theatrical events of the 1990s – Ron Vawter’s extraordinary performance piece ROY COHN/JACK SMITH – Godmilow crafts a dramatically deft, comic, and terrifying film diptych. Roy Cohn, the homophobic right-wing lawyer and sleazy back-room politico, thunders against the Sodom and Gomorrah of homosexuality at a banquet for the American Society for the Protection of the Family, while across town and light years away, the notorious underground filmmaker of FLAMING CREATURES fame, Jack Smith, in flamboyant harem drag, constructs his own private resistance theater from fragments of Arabian Nights kitsch, avant-garde film feuds, and passionate B-movie camp. Vawter performs both men exquisitely in this film about the closet, where silence is powerful, but from which both of these infamous homosexuals from the repressive and punishing 1950s convey privileged knowledge of Queerness in brilliant performances of their own – Cohn using politics as a form of drag and Smith turning drag into an extraordinary form of politics, pathos, and jouissance. Cohn and Smith had nothing in common except their homosexuality and their death from AIDS in the late 1980s; Vawter, who accepts and produces both men through his own voice and body, would himself die of AIDS, just six months after the film was shot.

title: After Hours
description: Cheech and Chong! Sultry sculptress Linda Fiorentino! Bad Brains! These are but a few of the characters that Midtown computer jockey Paul Hackett (Griffin Dunne) will encounter when venturing into the wilds of a pre-gentrification downtown New York without a penny to his name or the means to get back home in Scorsese’s bravura black comedy of class resentment, all-pervasive paranoia, and creeping castration anxiety, in which the director can be briefly spotted manning a spotlight at punk rock dive Club Berlin. As Dick Miller’s diner waiter explains to the hapless Hackett, “Different rules apply when it gets this late…” As true of the city in 1985 as it is today. Part of This Night Has Opened My Eyes

title: DRILLER KILLER
description:
A struggling painter in downtown Manhattan finds his creative frustrations compounded by financial pressure, intrusive roommates, and the relentless noise of a neighbouring punk band. As his psychological state deteriorates, the boundaries between artistic desperation and personal collapse erode, culminating in nocturnal escapades of violence that steadily overwhelm his grip on reality.
Positioned at the intersection of no-budget punk cinema and urban psychodrama, Driller Killer captures late-1970s New York at its most frayed—tense, impoverished, and artistically volatile. Ferrara’s portrait of creative burnout situates horror within the material conditions of the city, reflecting the economic precarity and cultural fragmentation that shaped the downtown scene.

description: Visionary director Jane Schoenbrun ( I Saw the TV Glow ) presents a new kind of horror remake in Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma . Bursting with imagination and surreal wit, their latest genre-bending wonder affirms there’s no such thing as a guilty pleasure.

title: Kill Bill: Vol. 1 on 35mm
description: Your Saturday night just got a whole lot more kick ass as Quentin Tarantino’s Kill Bill ignites our big screen with an onslaught of celluloid action! A former assassin, known simply as The Bride (Uma Thurman), wakes from a coma four years after her jealous ex-lover Bill (David Carradine) attempts to murder her on her wedding day. Fueled by an insatiable desire for revenge, she vows to get even with every person who contributed to the loss of her unborn child, her entire wedding party, and four years of her life. After devising a hit list, The Bride sets off on her quest, enduring unspeakable injury and unscrupulous enemies. So, hop in your p***ywagon and get ready for a maelstrom of revenge so bad ass and bloody, you might never recover!

title: DER FAN
description: Simone (the magnetic Désirée Nosbusch) is a teenage runaway who is obsessed with the pop singer known as “R.” Soon, that obsession takes over her life. When “R” uses Simone with machine-like coldness, she plots her revenge with an unholy ceremony that’s equally romantic and horrifying. Fueled by a killer minimalist synth soundtrack from Rheingold and a gorgeous design aesthetic, DER FAN is a subversive and electric shocker that goes harder than you’d ever expect it to go.

title: The Crow
description: People once believed that when someone dies, a crow carries their soul to the land of the dead. But sometimes, just sometimes, the crow can bring that soul back to put the wrong things right. The big screen goth fantasy update of James O’Barr’s comic follows a murdered musician resurrected to avenge his death and the killing of his fiancé. Featuring a soulful performance by the late Brandon Lee, stellar, rain-slicked cinematography by Dariusz Wolski, and a propulsive, chart-topping soundtrack featuring songs by The Cure, The Jesus and Mary Chain, Rage Against the Machine, Nine Inch Nails, Stone Temple Pilots, and more.

title: The Maltese Falcon             / The Petrified Forest
description: Everyone’s looking for it and they’ll do anything to get it! The Maltese Falcon , that is. It’s not just the opulent treasure in the mind’s eye of every San Francisco low-life, it’s also one of the first shining examples of Hollywood noir, a stunningly confident directing debut for John Huston, and a sordid melodrama which transformed Humphrey Bogart from B-movie sideman to star romantic lead. Mary Astor co-stars as the hot-blooded but inscrutable femme fatale who drags hard-boiled private eye Sam Spade (Bogart) into the hunt for the Falcon. Peter Lorre and Sydney Greenstreet (in his Academy Award-nominated film debut!) round out the conspiratorial cast as dandy-gangsters with twisted loyalties. The paradigm for film noir to come, this loaded, sordid mystery gets right to the tragic truth about love and crime: “It’s the stuff that dreams are made of.”

title: Spirited Away (English Dubbed)
description: Join us for a screening of the universally acclaimed and beloved animated film Spirited Away from Studio Ghibli and Hayao Miyazaki. A young girl, Chihiro, becomes trapped in a strange new world of spirits. When her parents undergo a mysterious porcine transformation, she must call upon the courage she never knew she had to free her family. A visually astounding feat of imagination and heart, this early-2000s brilliant and beautiful film was the first non-English language film to win the Academy Award for Best Animated Feature and is considered one of the greatest animated films of all time.

title: Onslaught

title: The Samurai and the Prisoner
description: Join us in the microcinema for Kiyoshi Kurosawa’s ponderous and philosophical samurai epic The Samurai and the Prisoner. When Lord Murashige rises up against the tyrannical Oda, he finds himself besieged within the walls of his own castle. Isolated, he is confronted with a series of mysterious crimes that shatter the fragile order of his court, plunging the fortress into fear and suspicion. With Oda’s army closing in and a traitor hiding among his ranks, Murashige is forced into an uneasy alliance with Kanbei, a brilliant and dangerous strategist held prisoner in the dungeon, as he must outwit his enemies and uncover the truth before time runs out.

title: Michael Waldron Presents BRIEF ENCOUNTER
description: Iconic director David Lean (LAWRENCE OF ARABIA, DOCTOR ZHIVAGO) deftly explores the thrill, pain and tenderness of an illicit romance in dour, gray post-war Britain. After a chance meeting on a train platform, a married doctor (Trevor Howard) and a suburban housewife (Celia Johnson) enter into a muted, passionate but ultimately unconsummated situationship. This depiction of powerful feelings kept under wraps is a definitive example of a particularly English style of emotional restraint. BRIEF ENCOUNTER is also a potent beacon for queer subtext, as its subject of forbidden love holds special resonance.

title: Mutts
description: Mutts. 2019. Canada. Directed by Halima Ouardiri. DCP. 18 min. Man Push Cart. 2005. USA. Written and directed by Ramin Bahrani. With Ahmad Razvi, Leticia Dolera, Charles Daniel Sandoval. 35mm. 87 min. Inspired by lead actor Ahmad Razvi’s life story, Ramin Bahrani’s Man Push Cart offers a melancholic look at post-9/11 New York from the perspective of a Pakistani immigrant—a former rock star in his native country, now a widower estranged from his son in Pakistan—as he struggles to make a living selling coffee and bagels, dragging a heavy cart through the cold, impersonal streets of Midtown Manhattan. Two decades later, Bahrani’s celebrated debut film remains a subtle look at the lives of those pushed to the margins of the American dream in a city marked by a lack of human connection. In Mutts, Halima Ouardiri films a large sanctuary in Morocco, filled with hundreds of stray dogs, and uses it as a metaphor for the struggles of refugees and life in poverty and confinement.

title: Pee-wee’s Big Adventure
description: The story of a rebel and his bike. In Tim Burton’s dynamite feature length directorial debut, Pee-wee Herman explodes to life in one of the most exciting, creatively colorful, constantly quotable and enduring comedies of the decade! When his fully customized, fire engine red bicycle is stolen, Pee-wee sets off on a Big Adventure to get it back, hitchhiking cross-country and encountering a quirky cast of new friends along the way.

title: Top Hat
description: An American tap dancer pursues the woman he loves from London to Venice in the fourth movie musical to feature the iconic team of Fred Astaire and Ginger Rogers, and the second of their films to receive a Best Picture nomination, following The Gay Divorcee (1934). Spotlighting the stars at their effortless best, it was also nominated for Irving Berlin’s classic “Cheek to Cheek,” Hermes Pan’s dance direction of the numbers “Piccolino” and “Top Hat, White Tie, and Tails,” and the art direction of Van Nest Polglase and Carroll Clark, whose elegant deco sets include a Venice canal constructed on a Los Angeles soundstage.

title: THE PIANO
description: When an arranged marriage brings Ada and her spirited daughter to the wilderness of nineteenth-century New Zealand, she finds herself locked in a battle of wills with both her controlling husband and a rugged frontiersman to whom she develops a forbidden attraction.

title: Off-Circuit: UK PREMIERE Pin de Fartie + Q&A
description: The latest production from boundlessly imaginative Argentine collective El Pampero Cine sees successive pairs of characters bid farewell: a mother and her son, a caretaker and her charge, two actors endlessly rehearsing a scene that will never be performed. A playful spin on theatrical adaptation, Alejo Moguillansky's new film is a delightfully imaginative take on Samuel Beckett's Fin de Partie , punctuated by music, tennis, and another exceptional turn by Laura Paredes. The UK Premiere screening on the 4 September will be followed by an in-person Q&A with Alejo Moguillansky.

title: ALGIERS: The Pan African-Festival of Algiers 1969 (15)
Rio Archive Martial Arts Cinema Culture Panel
description: THIS EVENT IS FREE  A panel of special guests discuss martial arts films in respect of the history of Rio Cinema and its history of showing martial arts films in the past. We get to see a reel provided by Rio Cinema and some slides and clips of some old classic martial arts films.

title: VIDEOHEAVEN
description:
A cultural history of the video rental store told entirely through its appearances in film and television, tracing how the rise of VHS transformed the way audiences discovered, consumed, and thought about movies. Drawing on hundreds of clips spanning decades of popular culture, the documentary charts the birth, evolution, decline, and lasting legacy of the video store as both a physical space and a cinematic icon.
Rather than relying on interviews, the film unfolds as a feature-length visual essay, using an expansive collage of archive footage, commercials, and scenes from Hollywood and independent cinema to examine how video stores shaped movie culture. By treating the video shop as a social space, a workplace, and a recurring screen setting, it becomes both a history of home video and a reflection on the changing relationship between audiences and cinema.

title: The Seven Year Itch
description: We’re celebrating 100 years of one of the biggest icons of the silver screen – Marilyn Monroe – with a special screening of Billy Wilder’s hilarious classic comedy The Seven Year Itch . Laugh yourself silly with this beloved comedy of infatuation and infidelity starring Marilyn in her most-remembered roles (and dresses!). When his family goes away for summer vacation, a hitherto faithful publishing executive with an overactive imagination is tempted by an attractive new neighbor. With pitch-perfect delivery, and her effortless charm – not too mention her most notable pose on a sewer grate – it isn’t hard to see why Marilyn Monroe continues to captivate 100 years after her birth (as Norma Jean Baker) and over 60 years after her tragic death.

title: THE LITTLE DEATHS / LAS MUERTES CHIQUITAS
description: “In 2006 the Barcelona artist and filmmaker Mireia Sallarès began interviewing, in complete intimacy, about thirty Mexican women, about just that: being women in Mexico and their sexual experiences – their experience with pleasure and also with violence. The result is LAS MUERTES CHIQUITAS, ‘the little deaths’, which, like the French ‘la petite mort’, is a slangy euphemism in Spanish for female orgasm, the post-orgasmic state of unconsciousness that some experience after sex. This wild, five-hour film is revolutionary. […] Sallarès uses the simplest of means, filming by herself, entirely in medium close-ups, as she interviews, among many others, two anthropologists, a performance artist, an AIDS worker, a few sex-workers, a cabaret artist, two psychoanalysts, an historian, two ex-nuns, a journalist, a cross-dressing bisexual-tranny, a housekeeper, an actress, a philosopher, two guerillas, even exiled women from other countries…. She asks them to talk about, at first, their own orgasms. What emerge are extraordinary stories and images of pleasure, and often damage. “The film’s subtitle, ‘An unfinished story of pleasure and violence’, helps connect the dots. There is abundant sexual violence against and around women in Mexico, and effective resistance. Sallarès’s correspondents are prepared to talk about their histories and so the film goes there – not just to the violence but also to the relationship between violence and sexuality, and soon enough to violence, sex, pleasure and spiritual release. These are models to learn from and admire. The critic Helena Braunštajn says this film is a place ‘where pleasure is related to armed struggle, feminicide, transsexuality, women’s liberation theology, prostitution, illness, exile, the plurality of Mexican identity, and the ethical commitment of art to socio-political reality.’ One woman says orgasm is ‘like grabbing onto the wings of an angel who lowers me down to the ground.’ Enough said.” –Jill Godmilow

title: Transit
description: Transit. 2018. USA. Directed by Christian Petzold. Screenplay by Petzold, based on the book by Anna Seghers. With Franz Rogowski, Paula Beer, Godehard Giese. DCP. In German, French; English subtitles. 102 min. At the height of a European “migrant crisis,” Christian Petzold filmed an adaptation of Anna Seghers’s 1944 novel Transit, about a refugee who tries to escape a fascist police state by impersonating a dead writer. In a chilling, prescient move, Petzold masterfully blends past and present by filling the streets of Marseille with police, armed state forces, and political refugees, dressed in 21st-century attire, desperately trying to escape authoritarian repression.

title: CatVideoFest 2026
description: Our fuzzy overlords return to the big screen! Vidiots is purrfectly enthralled to bring back the cutest kitty compilation ever! CatVideoFest is a compilation reel of the latest and best cat videos culled from countless hours of unique submissions and sourced animations, music videos, and classic internet powerhouses. CatVideoFest is a joyous communal experience, only available in theaters, and raises money for cats in need through partnerships with local cat charities, animal welfare organizations, and shelters to best serve cats in the area.

Episodic, folkloric, and allegorical, it is a mythic search for hidden treasure by two brothers. Dovzhenko wrote: “I did not so much make the picture as sing it out like a songbird.”

title: TAKING OFF
description:
A teenage girl runs away from home, prompting her worried parents to search New York City for her. In the process, they become involved with a support group for parents of missing children and begin rediscovering themselves as they struggle to understand the widening gap between their generation and their daughter's.
Blending improvisation, gentle satire, and musical interludes, the film captures the cultural upheaval of early 1970s America with warmth and humour. Rather than taking sides, it observes both parents and teenagers with sympathy, finding comedy and poignancy in their mutual misunderstandings.

description: Miloš Forman directed Peter Shaffer’s screenplay, based on his Tony Award–winning play, about the 18th century rivalry between journeyman court composer Antonio Salieri (F. Murray Abraham in an Academy Award–winning tour de force) and young upstart Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart (fellow Best Actor nominee Tom Hulce). Saul Zaentz’s lavish production features opulent period details, while Shaffer’s witty script speaks eloquently about the challenge of art while leaving room for Mozart’s gorgeous music. The film earned 11 nominations, and its eight Oscar wins include Best Picture, Art Direction, Costume Design, Directing, Makeup, Sound, and for Shaffer’s adapted screenplay.

description: Willem Defoe plays Ed Saxberger, a forgotten New York poet, who works in the post office. After an eager and flattering young admirer appears on his doorstep, Saxberger is beckoned into a coterie of twentysomething admirers who anoint him as a rediscovered genius. Intoxicated by the attention — and by the alluring presence of Gloria, the group’s “tragic heroine” — Saxberger gradually reckons with the authenticity of his newfound poetic circle. Kent Jones's thoughtful, witty film is a wistful yet unromantic look at a lost idea of downtown New York.
