title: Salesman
description: This landmark documentary from Albert and David Maysles follows the bitter rivalry of four door-to-door salesmen working tirelessly to sell gold-embossed bibles . Times are tough for this hard-living quartet, who spend their days traveling through small-town America, trying their best to peddle gold-leaf Bibles to an apathetic crowd of lower-middle-class housewives and elderly couples. One of the most important and illuminating documentaries of the mid-20th-century, Salesman showed the world a realism it had never seen and a pair of brothers who would change the documentary landscape forever.
director: Albert Maysles, Charlotte Zwerin, David Maysles

title: LIFE STINKS
description: A wealthy businessman makes a bet he can survive homelessness on the L.A. streets for 30 days but quickly discovers it is much tougher than he imagined.

title: In-I In Motion + Q&A with Juliette Binoche
WHO WANTS TO KILL JESSIE?
description:
When scientist Růženka Beránková develops a machine capable of manipulating dreams, an experiment on her husband produces an unexpected consequence: characters from his favourite comic strip begin to materialise in the real world. Chief among them is Jessie, a glamorous heroine pursued by a superhuman strongman and a gun-toting cowboy. As the dream figures wander through Prague, leaving chaos in their wake, the boundaries between everyday reality and comic-book logic steadily collapse.
One of the great achievements of Czechoslovak popular cinema of the 1960s, Who Wants to Kill Jessie? combines science fiction, slapstick comedy, and comic-strip aesthetics into a playful satire of bureaucracy, technology, and mass media. Co-written by Miloš Macourek and featuring visual contributions from legendary comics artist Kája Saudek, the film brings speech balloons, sound effects, and graphic imagery directly into live-action space decades before such techniques became commonplace. Produced during the fertile period that also generated the Czech New Wave, it occupies a unique position between state-studio filmmaking, pop art experimentation, and fantastical genre cinema.

title: Filipiñana
description: Join us in the microcinema for one of the best films of the year and a masterwork of international cinema – Rafael Manuel’s phenomenally composed deadpan social satire Filipiñana . With jaw-dropping shot composition, immaculate color coding, a biting and satiric wit, and a slow deliberateness that builds to a shocking ending, this is a dazzler on another level with class consciousness to boot. If Ruben Ostlund and Wes Anderson had a Filipino baby, it still wouldn’t be as good as Filipiñana ! Don’t miss your chance to see this stunner on a big screen!

title: THE GLORIA OF YOUR IMAGINATION
description: “In 1964, an enterprising psychologist (Dr. Everett Shostrom) persuaded a 30-year-old waitress and single mother, to take part in filmed psychotherapy sessions, with three of the most influential psychologists of the 20th century. The resulting series, THREE APPROACHES TO PSYCHOTHERAPY (1965), was primary training material in the field for decades. With the immersive double projection of THE GLORIA OF YOUR IMAGINATION, Reeves creates an intricate, superimposed montage of Gloria’s unguarded sessions with numerous film artifacts of her lifetime: newsreels, home movies, commercials, a beauty pageant, Cold War propaganda, and educational films. The result sees viewers absorbing the culture of that era directly through Reeves’s mix of intimate storytelling and sense of curiosity.” –WEXNER CENTER FOR THE ARTS The screening on Fri, Sept 18 will involve 16mm + digital dual projection; the screenings on Sat & Sun, Sept 19 & 20 will be of the single-channel DCP version of the film.

title: MEISHI STREET
description: At the end of SPLITTING, a 1974 film recording of a building “cut” radical sculptor and architect Gordon Matta-Clark made to an abandoned family home in suburban New Jersey, the audience is told that the work was “demolished for urban ‘renewal’.” SPLITTING thus becomes an afterimage of a site-specific and self-destructive artistic thesis, but one that is nonetheless arresting in its visual expressiveness and solemn beauty. Conversely, in MEISHI STREET, Zhang Jinli fights tooth and nail to save his restaurant from demolition in preparation for the 2008 Beijing Olympics. Given a digital video camera by U-teque Collective member Ou Ning to document his efforts, Zhang turns the lens on himself as he makes and hangs protest banners outside his restaurant and visits neighbors, projecting the voice of his Dazhalan neighborhood into a condemned future. Preceded by: Gordon Matta-Clark SPLITTING 1974, 11 min, Super-8mm-to-digital, silent Total running time: ca. 100 min.

title: Fringe! Queer Film Festival presents: Two Times João Liberada + Three times Mina
description: Fringe! Queer Film Festival, in collaboration with Fruits on Film present: Two Times João Liberada + Three times Mina. Blurring the line between…

title: Blade Runner : Double Feature
description: BLADE RUNNER : THE FINAL CUT : Deckard (Harrison Ford) is forced by the police Boss (M. Emmet Walsh) to continue his old job as Replicant Hunter. His assignment: eliminate four escaped Replicants from the colonies who have returned to Earth. Before starting the job, Deckard goes to the Tyrell Corporation and he meets Rachel (Sean Young), a Replicant girl he falls in love with. BLADE RUNNER 2049 : Officer K (Ryan Gosling), a new blade runner for the Los Angeles Police Department, unearths a long-buried secret that has the potential to plunge what's left of society into chaos. His discovery leads him on a quest to find Rick Deckard (Harrison Ford), a former blade runner who's been missing for 30 years. Please Note: We will be running the films with a short 10min break between. We would ask that you remain in your seat for the duration of this break.

title: The Fall - 20th Anniversary
description: A bedridden patient in a hospital on the outskirts of 1920s Los Angeles befriends a fellow patient, and shares a fantastic tale of heroes, myths, and villains on a desert island with the little girl.

title: My Cousin Vinny
description: Two carefree pals traveling through rural Alabama on their way back to college are mistakenly arrested and charged with murder. Fortunately, one of them has a cousin who’s a lawyer – Vincent Gambini, a former auto mechanic from Brooklyn who has just passed his bar exam after his sixth try. When he arrives with his leather-clad girlfriend to try his first case, it’s a real shock – for him and the Deep South!

title: WHO ARE YOU, POLLY MAGGOO?
description:
A television crew follows Polly Maggoo, an American supermodel living in Paris, as part of a documentary attempting to uncover the person behind her public image. While the crew investigates her life, Polly navigates the attention of the fashion world, admirers, and men who project their own fantasies onto her. (IMDb)
William Klein’s satirical mockumentary takes aim at the absurdity of fashion, celebrity culture, and the media’s obsession with image and personality. Blending pop art, surreal humour, and documentary techniques, it captures the artificial world of 1960s fashion while questioning whether anyone can truly exist outside the images created around them.

title: Minority Report
description: An all-too prescient science fiction blockbuster of the surveillance state gone awry, Steven Spielberg’s adaptation of Philip K. Dick is a dystopian thriller for this and any time! Set in Washington D.C. in 2054, where police utilize a psychic technology to arrest and convict murderers before they commit their crime. Tom Cruise plays the head of this Precrime unit and is himself accused of the future murder of a man he hasn’t even met. With the blockbuster action you’ve come to expect from Spielberg, and the dystopian cynicism of Philip K. Dick, Minority Report remains a big screen banger with a brain and a message that only gets more timely as our own surveillance state increases!

title: Doc'n Roll: HAKEEM (+ Q&A and Acoustic Set)
description: Doc'n Roll presents HAKEEM (+ Q&A and Acoustic Set) dir. DEADHORSES | UK | 2024  Doc’n Roll is delighted to be part of The Music is Black Festival from East Bank and to bring a special event to the Rio Cinema celebrating one of London’s most distinctive contemporary musicians, Hak Baker.  The evenin...

title: TCM's The Plot Thickens Presents DR. STRANGELOVE
description: Psychotic Air Force General Jack D. Ripper (Sterling Hayden) unleashes an ingenious, foolproof and irrevocable scheme sending bombers to attack Russia. Meanwhile, U.S. President Muffley (Peter Sellers) works with the Soviet Ambassador (Peter Bull) in a desperate effort to save the world. Featuring George C. Scott, Keenan Wynn, Slim Pickens and a 33-year-old James Earl Jones in his feature film debut as Lt. Lothar Zogg.

title: THIS IS SPINAL TAP
description: Conceived by comedy greats Rob Reiner, Christopher Guest, Michael McKean and Harry Shearer, THIS IS SPINAL TAP chronicles one of England’s loudest bands on what proves to be a disastrous U.S. tour.

title: Outerlands
description: Join us in the microcinema for Elena Oxman’s festival darling, the beautifully touching triumph Outerlands starring Asia Kate Dillon in a stirring performance. Cass juggles jobs as a nanny, restaurant server, and party drug dealer to make ends meet and pay for their tiny San Francisco apartment. After a one night stand with Kalli, a co-worker they have a crush on, Cass agrees to watch her 11-year-old daughter, Ari, while she goes out of town. But as days pass without word from Kalli, Cass and Ari form a bond that spirals Cass back to their own difficult childhood and the pain they’ve been running from. With beautiful cinematography and an exploration of a San Francisco seldom celebrated, this little charmer is a warm and wonderful treat.

title: Fight Club
description: The first rule of Fight Club is: You do not talk about Fight Club . David Fincher’s stylized adaptation of the Chuck Palahniuk book is a darkly comic and intoxicatingly energetic screen thunderbolt, a visually striking, critically polarizing, and often misunderstood exploration of modern-day man, mischief, madness, mayhem and soap. Brad Pitt, Edward Norton, and Helena Bonham Carter turn in powerful performances, while the Dust Brothers provide a propulsive score.

title: NO OTHER LAND
description: Rather than engendering solidarity and empathy through the depiction of destruction of social and material Palestinian life in the present tense, Cynthia Madansky’s STILL LIFE chooses instead to take spectators on a tour of the Occupied Territories after the bulldozers have rumbled through and the bombs have fallen. Hanging its power on aftermath, STILL LIFE reaches instead for a set of festering implications and associations triggered via images, musical composition, and spoken questions. Like many of the other films in this series, NO OTHER LAND preserves in the visual archive what will likely be lost. Shot over the course of five years and by a collective of four directors from Palestine and Israel, NO OTHER LAND shocks in its immediacy and palpable danger as an SOS call from Masafer Yatta, a front line of the Palestinian struggle. Preceded by: Cynthia Madansky STILL LIFE 2004, 15 min, Super-8mm-to-digital. Sound design by Zeena Parkins. Total running time: ca. 110 min.
director: Yuval Abraham, Basel Adra, Hamdan Ballal, and Rachel Szor

title: WHEN IT WAS BLUE
description: WHEN IT WAS BLUE rejoices in the splendor of nature as the camera eye traverses land and sea in a montage of diverse ecosystems from the Americas to Iceland and New Zealand. Reeves creates colorful, organic textures and forms, inspired by elements of the natural world, using an array of direct-on-film techniques. This abstract imagery is superimposed upon wildlife footage, generating depth while merging the powerful intricacies of nature with an artist’s reverence for it. With her Bolex, Reeves hurries to “capture” the natural world before it vanishes. An original score by Reeves’s collaborator, composer and performer Skúli Sverrisson, transports the audience to a realm at once haunting, urgent, and rapturous.

title: Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind
description: After a painful breakup, Clementine (Kate Winslet) undergoes a procedure to erase memories of her former boyfriend Joel (Jim Carrey) from her mind. When Joel discovers that Clementine is going to extremes to forget their relationship, he undergoes the same procedure and slowly begins to forget the woman that he loved. Directed by former music video director Michel Gondry, the visually arresting film explores the intricacy of relationships and the pain of loss.

title: MYSTERY MOVIE
description:
Not for the easily offended, and strictly programmed for adult audiences only - our mystery films are eye-popping forays into the bold and bonkers world of psychotronic cinema. Expect the unacceptable.
Please consider yourself forewarned that these films may (and probably will) contain offensive and upsetting content. Do not attend if you are of a sensitive disposition.

title: Heaven Knows What
description: Dropping you onto the heart of dirty NYC, like a bastard cross between THE PANIC IN NEEDLE PARK and CHRISTIANE F., this crushing story of a young junkie hooked on heroin and the wrong man, fellow addict and lover, Ilya, is a harrowing ride from start to finish. Based on an unpublished memoir from star Arielle Holmes, this frenetic anxiety-trip bops and weaves through the streets, assaults the senses with black metal needledrops, and leaves you jonesing for the next Safdie brothers fix.

title: Sgt. Pepper’s Lonely Hearts Club Band
description: Get ready for all the gonzo musical weirdness of this Beatles-tuned, Peter Frampton and the Bee Gees helmed cult classic of epic proportions! This musical, set to late-period Beatles hits, recounts the story of Sgt. Pepper’s famed musical group, which found success during World War I bringing music to weary soldiers in the field. The band’s leader has since died, and now it’s up to his grandson, Billy Shears (Peter Frampton), to carry on the group’s traditions. To this end, he recruits the Henderson brothers (Barry Gibb, Robin Gibb, Maurice Gibb) to help him defend the group’s magic instruments from nefarious crook B.D. Hoffler. It’s a bubblegum campfest head trip that is best experienced on the big screen with a crowd!

title: Fritz the Cat
description: We’re not rated X for nothin’, baby! Director Ralph Bakshi’s pushes the limits in his outrageous & groundbreaking feature length debut, a lewd & rude riot that helped shatter the notion of what animation could be. Adapted from the work of R. Crumb, this audaciously satirical adults-only fable follows a free-spirited anthropomorphic feline in a series of wild & debaucherous counter-culture adventures.

title: Free Willy
description: In this much-loved family classic, a 12-year-old orphaned boy named Jesse befriends a captive orca, Willy, at an ailing amusement park.…

title: Bloody Marys + When Harry Met Sally
description: On 20 September, members are invited to join us for a boozy brunch-time cocktail hour, followed by a lazy Sunday screening…

title: Barry Lyndon
description: Stanley Kubrick bent the conventions of the historical drama to his own will in this dazzling vision of a pitiless aristocracy, adapted from a novel by William Makepeace Thackeray. In picaresque detail, Barry Lyndon chronicles the adventures of an incorrigible trickster (Ryan O’Neal) whose opportunism takes him from an Irish farm to the battlefields of the Seven Years’ War and the parlours of high society. For the most sumptuously crafted film of his career, Kubrick recreated the decadent surfaces and intricate social codes of the period, evoking the light and texture of eighteenth-century painting with the help of pioneering cinematographic techniques and lavish costume and production design, all of which earned Academy Awards. The result is a masterpiece—a sardonic, devastating portrait of a vanishing world whose opulence conceals the moral vacancy at its heart. Please Note: The film will be presented with a brief 5-10min intermission.

title: Double Indemnity
description: In this classic film noir, insurance salesman Walter Neff (Fred MacMurray) gets roped into a murderous scheme when he falls for the sensual Phyllis Dietrichson (Barbara Stanwyck), who is intent on killing her husband (Tom Powers) and living off the fraudulent accidental death claim. Prompted by the late Mr. Dietrichson's daughter, Lola (Jean Heather), insurance investigator Barton Keyes (Edward G. Robinson) looks into the case, and gradually begins to uncover the sinister truth.

title: FRINGE PRESENTS: PROCESSING
description:
Processing takes film as a site of alchemy: a medium to be scratched, spliced, remixed and reanimated until its material grain becomes indistinguishable from memory itself. Across hand-processed Super 8, analogue video synthesis and found footage, this shorts programme interlaces the medium and materiality of queer film with desire and speculative futures; it refuses fixity.
As part of the screening, you are invited to take part in a cameraless 16mm filmmaking workshop. Working collaboratively through a series of material experiments, shared scores and collective processes, the group will scratch, draw on and rework film by hand. These experiments will be assembled into a short community film and screened as part of the programme.
Workshop: 60 min
Film Screening: 45 min

title: Encanto Sing-Along
description: One of Disney’s most delightful and beloved films of the 21st century, the animated fantasy Encanto is overflowing with unforgettable characters, colorful adventures, and hum-worthy tunes. The Madrigals are a family living in a mystical house in the mountains of Colombia, and each member of the clan has their own special power — all except for teen daughter Mirabel (voice of Stephanie Beatriz), still disappointed that she’s the only ordinary one. But when their magical world faces a new threat, Mirabel seizes her chance to be a hero after all. María Cecilia Botero, John Leguizamo, Mauro Castillo, Jessica Darrow, Diane Guerrero, and Wilmer Valderrama also lend their voices, and Lin-Manuel Miranda contributes eight original songs (including the impossibly catchy “We Don’t Talk About Bruno”). Sing along with this enchanted musical with your little ones, or your Pixar-loving adult besties!

title: Marketa Lazarová
description: Our screening on Friday 9 October will be introduced by Czech film expert Peter Hames. Voted the best Czech film ever…

title: The Incredible Journey (IB Tech Print)
description: Three against the wilderness… nothing could stop them – only instinct to guide them across 200 perilous miles of Canadian wilderness! An unlikely trio – a labrador retriever, bull terrier, and Siamese cat – must traverse treacherous terrain and overcome dangerous obstacles in their incredible journey home in Walt Disney’s fantastic real-life animal adventure.

title: Gigi
description: This lavish, widescreen musical from director Vincente Minnelli received nine Oscar nominations and won in each of its categories, including Best Picture and Directing. Minnelli’s An American in Paris (1951) discovery Leslie Caron plays Gigi, a young woman in turn-of-the-20th-century Paris who catches the eye of a charming womanizer (Louis Jourdan). The Oscar-winning screenplay by Alan Jay Lerner was based on the 1944 novella by Colette, and Lerner wrote the film’s original songs with his My Fair Lady (1964) composer Frederick Loewe, their score including such classics as “I Remember It Well,” “The Night They Invented Champagne,” and the Oscar-winning title song. Art directors William A. Horning and Preston Ames and set decorators Henry Grace and Keogh Gleason won Oscars for their eye-poppingly colorful recreation of the City of Light.

title: SHANE
description: Acclaimed director George Stevens’ legendary rendition of the quintessential Western myth earned six Academy Award nominations, and made SHANE one of the classics of the American cinema. The story brings Shane (Alan Ladd), a drifter and retired gunfighter, to the assistance of a homestead family terrorized by a wealthy cattleman and his hired gun (Jack Palance). In fighting the last decisive battle, Shane sees the end of his own way of life. Mysterious, moody and atmospheric, the film is enhanced by the intense performances of its splendid cast.

title: In The Mood For Love
description: In 1962 Hong Kong, neighbors Su Li-zhen (Mrs. Chan) and Chow Mo-wan (Mr. Chow) discover their spouses are having an affair. As they spend time together, they develop feelings for each other, but their relationship remains chaste and unspoken, reflecting societal constraints and their own moral compass.

title: MYSTERY DOJO: SURPRISE KUNG FU MATINEES
description:
Enter the 36 Chambers of Grindhouse Cinema, with these Sunday mystery martial-arts matinees that harken back to the glory days of 42nd Street.
Expect deep-cut chopsocky plucked from the 70s and 80s screening on both digital and VHS - with bone-crushing bashers from the genre that mixed Chinese folklore and fantasy, spaghetti westerns, melodrama, Japanese samurai films and American genre cinema into an electrifying combo that inspired both the future of action films - and hip hop.
These Kung Fu flicks became an international sensation in the 1970s, particularly at the Grindhouse cinemas that proliferated in impoverished inner-cities. Here were movies in which working-class heroes stood up to oppression, speaking loud and clear to the marginalised underclasses around the world.
Bring the ruckus!

title: The Transformers: The Movie: 40th Anniversary
description: TICKETS ON SALE TO MEMBERS 7th AUGUST 9AM / ON SALE TO EVERYONE 8th AUGUST 9AM In 1986, THE TRANSFORMERS: THE MOVIE rolled into cinemas and changed the franchise forever. Unicron arrives as a planet-sized threat to the universe, heroes rise, legends are forged and an entire generation of kids were changed forever by THAT moment, which still hits like a truck. Featuring an iconic voice cast, unforgettable animation and a soundtrack that hadabsolutely no business going that hard, the film remains one of the boldest animated classics of its era. Now, forty years later, it returns to the big screen in 4K for a special anniversary celebration of the battle, the music and the legacy. Stay through the credits...because as this journey ends, a new one begins. Features 10-15 mins of never-before-seen exclusive content!

title: IN VANDA’S ROOM / NO QUARTO DA VANDA
description: The second in his Fontainhas trilogy, IN VANDA’S ROOM follows heroin addict Vanda Duarte and a group of struggling slum dwellers as they try to make a life amid the demolition of their Lisbon neighborhood. Between Vanda’s raucous coughing fits and the clicks of her butane lighter, Costa’s extreme long takes, filmed in austere digital video, capture the sound of her built environs collapsing around her. Unlike the Barcelona neighborhood in EN CONSTRUCCIÓN, though, Fontainhas was wiped from the map by city officials, irredeemable in the eyes of the state, its inhabitants moved elsewhere. Today, it no longer stands, but remains embalmed in the images of Costa’s film. IN VANDA’S ROOM probes the limit of what cinema is and is capable of, not only in its content, which is bleak and harrowing to be sure, but in its form. Like many films in this series, it is uninterested in the distinction between fiction and documentary, choosing instead to capture life in its essence by whatever means necessary. André Bazin wrote that photography, and by extension cinema, satisfied the deep need that man had for an image that was not an approximation, but was the object itself, “freed from the conditions of time and space that govern it.” Sometimes, truth must be freed from the conditions of the objectively real: Costa proclaimed that he filmed some scenes multiple times until they “became fluidly represented and detached of any melodramatic tone.” Often, truth requires some coaxing.

title: An Evening with Mike Mills – Beginners
description: Vidiots is thrilled to welcome Indie legend Mike Mills for an enchanting night of cinema starting with the lovable modern classic Beginners followed by a conversation with Mills.

title: JENNIFER REEVES SHORT FILM PGM
description: This program is anchored by the 1996 film CHRONIC, which combines documentary and found footage with scripted scenes (featuring Reeves herself, as well as filmmakers Joe Gibbons, Jeannie Liotta, and Joel Schlemowitz) to form an experimental narrative about a young woman who began mutilating herself as a girl to cope with a traumatic mid-western girlhood. The program also includes early 16mm works like TASTE IT NINE TIMES and THE GIRL’S NERVY, video pieces such as SKINNY TEETH and the previously unseen MOTHERS’ DAY, and an excerpt from a work-in-progress. TRAINS ARE FOR DREAMING (2009, 7 min, 16mm) CHRONIC (1996, 37.5 min, 16mm) FEAR OF BLUSHING (2001, 5.5 min, 16mm) TASTE IT NINE TIMES (1992, 5.5 min, 16mm) THE GIRL’S NERVY (1995, 5 min, 16mm) SKINNY TEETH (2001, 7 min, VHS-to-digital) [work-in-progress] (CELIA, DID YOU KNOW?) (2 min, video) MOTHER’S DAY (1988, 5 min, video) Total running time: ca. 80 min.

title: Le Samourai
description: After professional hitman Jef Costello is seen by witnesses his efforts to provide himself an alibi drive him further into a corner.

title: THE BEGUILED
description:
A wounded Union soldier, played by Clint Eastwood, is taken in by the inhabitants of a secluded Southern girls’ boarding school during the American Civil War. As he recovers under their care, the isolated household begins to shift in tone, with tension, jealousy, and suppressed desire slowly emerging beneath the surface of polite Southern hospitality.
Don Siegel constructs something quietly oppressive, letting the closed environment do most of the work as civility gradually erodes into manipulation and emotional volatility. What starts as a simple act of care becomes increasingly uneasy, with power constantly shifting between caretaker and captive.

title: Trainspotting - 30th Anniversary
description: Heroin addict Mark Renton (Ewan McGregor) stumbles through bad ideas and sobriety attempts with his unreliable friends -- Sick Boy (Jonny Lee Miller), Begbie (Robert Carlyle), Spud (Ewen Bremner) and Tommy (Kevin McKidd). He also has an underage girlfriend, Diane (Kelly Macdonald), along for the ride. After cleaning up and moving from Edinburgh to London, Mark finds he can't escape the life he left behind when Begbie shows up at his front door on the lam, and a scheming Sick Boy follows.

title: Single White Female
description: The screening will be introduced by Zodiac Film Club. They say looking for a roommate can be murder. This classic film…

title: An Evening with Mike Mills – C’mon C’mon
description: Our enchanting evening with Mike Mills continues with his latest intimate and tender triumph C’mon C’mon featuring an introduction by Mills.

title: THE GLORIA OF YOUR IMAGINATION
description: “In 1964, an enterprising psychologist (Dr. Everett Shostrom) persuaded a 30-year-old waitress and single mother, to take part in filmed psychotherapy sessions, with three of the most influential psychologists of the 20th century. The resulting series, THREE APPROACHES TO PSYCHOTHERAPY (1965), was primary training material in the field for decades. With the immersive double projection of THE GLORIA OF YOUR IMAGINATION, Reeves creates an intricate, superimposed montage of Gloria’s unguarded sessions with numerous film artifacts of her lifetime: newsreels, home movies, commercials, a beauty pageant, Cold War propaganda, and educational films. The result sees viewers absorbing the culture of that era directly through Reeves’s mix of intimate storytelling and sense of curiosity.” –WEXNER CENTER FOR THE ARTS The screening on Fri, Sept 18 will involve 16mm + digital dual projection; the screenings on Sat & Sun, Sept 19 & 20 will be of the single-channel DCP version of the film.

title: DEMOLITION / CHAIQIAN / 拆·迁
description: Using a waist-high camera pointed at the ground and a drone that follows above, Nadav Assor’s GROUND EFFECT takes its name from the phenomenon by which drones and helicopters, in the process of mapping the environment, alter the landscape by displacing the ground’s surface. The objective visual recording thus becomes subjective in its effect on the land. Merging the camera footage into one, Assor points out the unique flaws and irreconcilability of objective and subjective ways of perceiving. Likewise, J.P. Sniadecki’s DEMOLITION / CHAIQIAN, produced in association with the Harvard Sensory Ethnography Lab, shakes loose a firm cinematic sense of perception. Shot over the course of three weeks and following a group of migrant demolition workers and city dwellers in Chengdu, China, DEMOLITION / CHAIQIAN imbues heavy demolition equipment with awkwardness and humor and turns cameras on cameras, all while a city is disappearing underfoot amidst a sonic tank of grinding metal, bursting concrete, and electronic beeps. Conversely, in Viktoria Schmid’s W O W (KODAK), structures reappear as demolished portions of the Rochester Kodak factory emerge from towering dust clouds, rhyming with the Lumière brothers’ DEMOLITION D’UN MUR made over a century prior. Preceded by: Viktoria Schmid W O W (KODAK) 2018, 2 min, 35mm-to-DCP Nadav Assor GROUND EFFECT 2016, 14 min, digital Total running time: ca. 85 min.

title: In-I In Motion + Q&A with Juliette Binoche
One Flew Over The Cuckoo's Nest
description: Adapted from Ken Kesey’s novel, the film centres on Randle McMurphy (Nicholson), a convict who simulates mental illness in the hope that a transfer to psychiatric hospital might ensure his early release. But he hasn’t bargained for the rigid regimen of Nurse Ratched (Louise Fletcher, also superb), who dislikes his disruptive — though he’d say liberating — effect on the ward. Inspired casting (Danny DeVito, Brad Dourif and Christopher Lloyd are among the patients) and Forman’s naturalistic direction lend authenticity to the proceedings, so that the film succeeds both as anti-authoritarian parable and as an affecting reminder of the psychiatric practices of the past.

title: Filipiñana
description: Join us in the microcinema for one of the best films of the year and a masterwork of international cinema – Rafael Manuel’s phenomenally composed deadpan social satire Filipiñana . With jaw-dropping shot composition, immaculate color coding, a biting and satiric wit, and a slow deliberateness that builds to a shocking ending, this is a dazzler on another level with class consciousness to boot. If Ruben Ostlund and Wes Anderson had a Filipino baby, it still wouldn’t be as good as Filipiñana ! Don’t miss your chance to see this stunner on a big screen!

title: Cinema Paradiso [Nuovo Cinema Paradiso]
description: A winner of awards across the world including Best Foreign Language Film Oscar, 5 BAFTA Awards including Best Actor, Original Screenplay and Score, the Grand Prize of the Jury at the Cannes Film Festival and many more. Giuseppe Tornatore's loving homage to the cinema tells the story of Salvatore, a successful film director, returning home for the funeral of Alfredo, his old friend who was the projectionist at the local cinema throughout his childhood. Soon memories of his first love affair with the beautiful Elena and all the highs and lows that shaped his life come flooding back, as Salvatore reconnects with the community he left 30 years earlier.

title: PLAY MISTY FOR ME
description:
A late-night radio DJ in California becomes the target of an increasingly obsessive fan who begins inserting herself into his personal life. What starts as flirtatious contact escalates into stalking, emotional manipulation, and escalating violence that disrupts both his relationships and sense of safety.
Clint Eastwood’s directorial debut leans into a taut psychological thriller structure, using its coastal California setting and radio broadcast framework to build intimacy and unease at the same time. The film steadily tightens its focus as admiration curdles into fixation, turning everyday encounters into sources of threat.

title: KING LEAR
description: As the world recovers from the destruction of the Chernobyl disaster, William Shakespeare Jr. the Fifth (Peter Sellars) attempts to restore the human race’s great works of art. His quest takes him to a hotel in Switzerland where he meets an old gangster (Burgess Meredith) and his daughter, Cordelia (Molly Ringwald). William’s journey also leads him to encounters with an absurd professor (Jean-Luc Godard) and an unhinged filmmaker (Woody Allen).

title: The Unknown (1927)(Silent with Live Music Score)             / Outside the Law (1920)(Silent with Live Music Score)
description: A criminal on the run conceals his identity by becoming Alonzo the Armless, a carnival act who uses his feet to throw knives. But when the daughter of the circus owner catches his eye, he’ll go to extreme measures to win her affections. Lon Chaney, Joan Crawford, and Norman Kerry star in a startling & unforgettable silent classic from Freaks director Tod Browning.

title: Inland Empire
description: An actress's perception of reality becomes increasingly distorted as she finds herself falling for her co-star in a remake of an unfinished Polish production that was supposedly cursed.

title: Gloria
description: When a young boy's family is killed by the mob, their tough neighbor Gloria becomes his reluctant guardian. In possession of a book that the gangsters want, the pair go on the run in New York.

title: How to Marry a Millionaire
description: Schatze, Pola, and Loco (Lauren Bacall, Marilyn Monroe, Betty Grable) are Manhattan models on a mission to marry rich husbands. Although they set their sights on Vanderbilts and Rockefellers, their plans go awry when they become attracted to men who look to be penniless. How to Marry a Millionaire was released at the end of Monroe’s breakout year, having starred in Gentlemen Prefer Blondes and Niagara in 1953. The film is notable as the first to be completed in CinemaScope, and Monroe had such broad appeal that 20th Century-Fox used her to advertise this new widescreen format: a slogan above an image of Marilyn claimed she was “Big as life and a million times more fun in Cinemascope!”

title: On the Silver Globe
description: The screening on August 22nd will feature an introduction by writer Daniel Bird. Subsequent screenings of On the Silver Globe will feature…

title: Amarcord
description: In an Italian seaside town, young Titta gets into trouble with his friends and watches various local eccentrics as they engage in often absurd behavior. Frequently clashing with his stern father and defended by his doting mother, Titta witnesses the actions of a wide range of characters, from his extended family to Fascist loyalists to sensual women, with certain moments shifting into fantastical scenarios.

title: Sexy Beast
description: Ex-villain Gal Dove (Ray Winstone) has served his time behind bars and is blissfully retired to a Spanish villa paradise with a wife he adores. The idyll is shattered by the arrival of his gangster nemesis Don Logan (Ben Kingsley), intent on persuading Gal to return to London for one last big job. Desperate not to sacrifice his enchanted existence, Dove is drawn into a shocking and explosive battle of wills with Logan, and takes part in a sensational underwater heist, risking everything to protect the woman he loves.

title: Legend (1985)
description: * ON SALE 23rd AUG * Set in a timeless mythical forest inhabited by fairies, goblins, unicorns and mortals, this fantastic story follows a mystical forest dweller, chosen by fate, to undertake a heroic quest. He must save the beautiful Princess Lili and defeat the demonic Lord of Darkness, or the world will be plunged into a never-ending ice age.

title: The Transformers: The Movie: 40th Anniversary
description: TICKETS ON SALE TO MEMBERS 7th AUGUST 9AM / ON SALE TO EVERYONE 8th AUGUST 9AM In 1986, THE TRANSFORMERS: THE MOVIE rolled into cinemas and changed the franchise forever. Unicron arrives as a planet-sized threat to the universe, heroes rise, legends are forged and an entire generation of kids were changed forever by THAT moment, which still hits like a truck. Featuring an iconic voice cast, unforgettable animation and a soundtrack that hadabsolutely no business going that hard, the film remains one of the boldest animated classics of its era. Now, forty years later, it returns to the big screen in 4K for a special anniversary celebration of the battle, the music and the legacy. Stay through the credits...because as this journey ends, a new one begins. Features 10-15 mins of never-before-seen exclusive content!

title: DOOR
description:
A housewife named Yasuko lives with her husband and young son in a high‑rise apartment, where a persistent door‑to‑door salesman begins to harass her after she accidentally injures him trying to keep him outside. The unwanted encounters quickly escalate into threatening phone calls, disturbing messages on her front door, and a growing sense that her everyday life is slipping into paranoia and danger. As the salesman’s behaviour becomes more unsettling, the tension widens into a nightmarish battle for control of her own home.
This 1988 Japanese horror thriller builds dread out of ordinary life disrupted by obsession and intrusion, moving from quiet unease to increasingly intense scenes of psychological and physical threat. Known for its raw atmosphere and relentless pacing, Door has become a cult rediscovery for fans of classic J‑horror rooted in fear that starts at the threshold of home.

title: Cinematic Void Presents EFFECTS
description: Recently Deceased Media merch will be available for purchase prior to the screening.

title: STILL LIFE / 三峡好人
description: If Jia Zhangke’s breakout film PLATFORM (2000) was about the destruction of China’s social fabric as it transitioned from Mao to Deng Xiaoping, then Jia’s 2006 Golden Lion winner STILL LIFE focuses on the physical destruction of the built environment as the country ventures through another epochal shift. Like Ou Ning’s MEISHI STREET, STILL LIFE is firmly located during what Western observers routinely note as the era of a “rising China.” A few years after the country’s admittance to the WTO, a couple years before Beijing hosted the 2008 Olympics, and during a time of rising GDP, STILL LIFE asks, in literal terms, whether a rising tide indeed lifts all boats. Shot on location in Fengjie, a town along the Yangtze River in central China, the film centers on two people as they search for their spouses in the city, slowly being demolished to make way for the Three Gorges Dam. Slated to be flooded by the dam’s reservoir, the town is replete with hand painted red lines on the sides of buildings that indicate the imminent water levels, offering a stark warning for those below the line to get out while they can. Like Pedro Costa’s IN VANDA’S ROOM, STILL LIFE is filmed on digital video, lending it not only a documentary aesthetic (emblematic of the Urban Generation of Chinese independent filmmakers at the time), but one of uncanny immediacy. Jia, embracing the xianchang spirit of on-the-ground filmmaking, has argued that the documentarian must allow themself to be “seared” by the immediate present. The traces of the people and buildings of Fengjie, though now relocated and demolished, respectively, become irrevocably imprinted on STILL LIFE and its maker.

title: The Lord of the Rings: The Two Towers [Theatrical Cut]
description: Frodo Baggins and the other members of the Fellowship continue on their sacred quest to destroy the One Ring--but on separate paths. Their destinies lie at two towers--Orthanc Tower in Isengard, where the corrupt wizard Saruman awaits, and Sauron's fortress at Barad-dur, deep within the dark lands of Mordor. Frodo and Sam are trekking to Mordor to destroy the One Ring of Power while Gimli, Legolas and Aragorn search for the orc-captured Merry and Pippin. All along, nefarious wizard Saruman awaits the Fellowship members at the Orthanc Tower in Isengard.

title: Boogie Nights
description: In the San Fernando Valley in 1977, teenage busboy Eddie Adams (Mark Wahlberg) gets discovered by porn director Jack Horner (Burt Reynolds), who transforms him into adult-film sensation Dirk Diggler. Brought into a supportive circle of friends, including fellow actors Amber Waves (Julianne Moore), Rollergirl (Heather Graham) and Reed Rothchild (John C. Reilly), Dirk fulfills all his ambitions, but a toxic combination of drugs and egotism threatens to take him back down.

title: A NEW LOVE IN TOKYO
description:
Part whip-smart hangout comedy, part pink film erotica. A New Love in Tokyo follows Rei, an aspiring actor and professional dominatrix, as she splits her time between rehearsing experimental theatre, hanging out with her friend Ayumi - a call girl, and gleefully dominating her clients in the dungeon.
Marketed in some territories (and still occasionally referred to) as ‘Tokyo Decadence 2’, A New Love in Tokyo stands distinct as an unashamedly joyous, charming, and sexually-charged work. Directed by pinku/V-cinema legend Banmei Takahashi (Door, Door II), and shot with an energetic, moody atmosphere. Don’t miss the rare chance to catch this newly restored pink cinema classic on the big screen.
Programmed and introduced by film critic Alexander Sternberg

title: GUMMO
description: With strains of his nihilistic youth-culture script for Larry Clark’s KIDS, Harmony Korine’s directorial debut moves out of the city to wander the post-apocalyptic fallout of a suburban Midwestern landscape recently ravaged by a tornado. Weaving between the day-to-day lives of various poverty-stricken small-town outcasts, GUMMO’s scattershot structure and varied shooting styles present a collage of American themes on the precipice of an unpredictable new millennium, ultimately yielding a movie that Gus Van Sant called “both bracingly realistic and hauntingly dreamlike.”

title: The Thing with Two Heads             / The Black Gestapo
description: They transplanted a white bigot’s head onto a soul brother’s body! The doctor blew it – the most fantastic medical experiment of the age. And now, with the fights, the fuzz, the chicks and the choppers… man, they’re really in deeeeep trouble! Ray Milland and Rosey Grier star in a raucously entertaining grindhouse great directed by exploitation legend Lee Frost.

title: The Matrix
description: When a beautiful stranger leads computer hacker Neo to a forbidding underworld, he discovers the shocking truth--the life he knows is the elaborate deception of an evil cyber-intelligence.

title: Days Of Being Wild
description: Yuddy, a Hong Kong playboy known for breaking girls' hearts, tries to find solace and the truth after discovering the woman who raised him isn't his mother.

title: April X
description: When his twin sister April (Lilly Krug) goes missing, Bax (Connor Storrie) searches every corner of their futuristic, post-Soviet cityscape to find her, ultimately descending into madness.

title: Daisies
description: Our screening on Thursday 8 October will be introduced by art historian and Fashion in Film Festival director Marketa Uhlirova. A…

title: Phantom of the Paradise
description: After record producer Swan (Paul Williams) steals the music of songwriter Winslow Leach (William Finley) and gives it to one of his bands, Leach sneaks into Swan's offices. Catching Leach, Swan frames him for dealing drugs, which lands him in prison. After Leach breaks out and again attempts to sabotage Swan's empire, an accident crushes his face. Leach then dons a costume and becomes the Phantom, intent on ruining Swan while saving singer Phoenix (Jessica Harper) from a terrible fate.

title: Angel's Egg
description: In an underwater city, a young girl takes care of a large egg she holds carefully in her arms. A boy with a gun arrives in search of a bird he saw in his dream. At first, it seems as if feelings of sympathy are developing between the two. Forty years after the film’s original release, Anime Limited is proud to present an all-new 4K restoration of the film, supervised by director Mamoru Oshii, in cinemas nationwide for the very first time. The film is a creative collaboration between acclaimed director Mamoru Oshii (Ghost in the Shell), who wrote and directed the feature, and revered artist Yoshitaka Amano (Final Fantasy, Vampire Hunter D). The film beautifully intertwines Oshii’s thematic reflections on philosophy and theology with Amano’s distinctive ink painting style, culminating in an arrestingly beautiful hand-drawn allegorical fantasy.

title: In-I In Motion + Q&A with Juliette Binoche
RUBBLE ON SCREEN: SHORT FILM PGM
description: The final program of the series is comprised of shorts that condense the myriad affects elucidated by the preceding works. Here, the wrecking ball and excavator become central players as humans largely exit the drama, leaving inanimate objects the task of carrying high tragedy and comedy. In Milèna Trivier’s elegiac 12 AUGUST 2002, the filmmaker frames the demolition of a brick gable from below and against the sky, a towering sentinel pummeled, its pieces sold for scrap. Conversely, in Jacob Burckhardt’s playful JawwZZZ, bright orange excavators lose their menace and become bumbling figures as they devour concrete and shift twisted metal, construction crews hosing down the creatures as zookeepers would elephants. Critique remains pointed though in Dominic Angerame’s IN THE COURSE OF HUMAN EVENTS, an anti-city symphony that, instead of celebrating the triumphs of urban technological progress, explores the remnants of de-industrialization in a black and white moonscape bereft of human presence. William Raban TIME STEPPING (1974, 19 min, 16mm-to-digital) Dominic Angerame IN THE COURSE OF HUMAN EVENTS (1997, 23 min, 16mm) Miléna Trivier 12 AUGUST 2002 (2002, 10 min, video. Voiceover by John Berger.) Anna Thew LFMC DEMOLITION (2004, 9 min, 16mm-to-digital) Jacob Burckhardt JawwZZZ (2024, 15 min, digital. Soundtrack by Lary 7.) Louis Lumière & Auguste Lumière DEMOLITION OF A WALL / DÉMOLITION D’UN MUR (1895, 1.5 min, 35mm-to-DCP) Total running time: ca. 85 min.

title: G.B.H.
description:
A former boxer turned nightclub bouncer is drawn back into a world of violence when he is hired to protect an upmarket Manchester club. As rival criminals attempt to take control of the business, he finds himself caught between gang warfare, loyalty, and survival.
A rough-edged British crime thriller from the early 1980s, the film belongs to the independent gangster cinema that emerged outside the mainstream, with a gritty northern setting and a focus on nightclub culture, intimidation, and street-level violence. Its low-budget atmosphere and exploitation influences make it a curiosity for fans of British crime cinema.

title: VALENTIN NOUJAÏM PGM 1: VEILED STRUGGLES
description: VEILED STRUGGLES: QUEERNESS, COLONIALISM, AND MEMORY Valentin Noujaïm OCEANIA 2024, 24 min, digital. In French with English subtitles. Sixteen-year-old Najib luxuriates in his summer days of gaming until his mother informs him of a neighbor’s passing. Taking the keys to their apartment, he quickly discovers an unexpected world of painful questions. “OCEANIA is an ode to tenderness. To a new generation that carries on our struggles, that seeks to remember whilst also moving forward. A tribute to love, to the dead and martyrs, and to present history being dismantled and destroyed.” –Valentin Noujaïm Richard Fung SEA IN THE BLOOD 2000, 26 min, video “SEA IN THE BLOOD was to be a meditation on race, sexuality and disease, but after working with the material for three years, it was the emotional story that came through. It’s hard to work with such personal material, but in the end the work takes on a life of its own. ‘Richard’ is a character. Because of the subject matter – disease and death – I wanted to avoid sentimentality. I’d like the audience to think as well as feel.” –Richard Fung Mohammed Soueid CINEMA FOUAD 1994, 28 or 41 min, video. In Arabic with English subtitles. A documentary on the life and ambitions of a young Lebanese trans woman, Khaled El Kurdi. The video follows her journey from soldier to cabaret dancer, in order to raise funds for her gender-affirming operation. Shot in Beirut, CINEMA FOUAD weaves a complex and multi-layered story of sexuality, identity, and desire, and paints a compelling portrait of its subject. Total running time: ca. 85 or 95 min. Followed by a conversation with writer and curator Adam HajYahia and Yasmina Price!

title: Filipiñana
description: Join us in the microcinema for one of the best films of the year and a masterwork of international cinema – Rafael Manuel’s phenomenally composed deadpan social satire Filipiñana . With jaw-dropping shot composition, immaculate color coding, a biting and satiric wit, and a slow deliberateness that builds to a shocking ending, this is a dazzler on another level with class consciousness to boot. If Ruben Ostlund and Wes Anderson had a Filipino baby, it still wouldn’t be as good as Filipiñana ! Don’t miss your chance to see this stunner on a big screen!

title: NT Live:The Misanthrope
description: Telling the truth isn't always that simple. Alice, a brilliant novelist, despises the carefully constructed lies of modern society. But the more she challenges those around her, the fiercer the backlash becomes. Soon, she must confront the price of speaking her truth in a world that would rather silence her. Filmed live on stage at the National Theatre, Indhu Rubasingham directs Martin Crimp's (Cyrano de Bergerac) highly anticipated play.

title: Celine and Julie Go Boating  [Céline et Julie vont en bateau]
description: A mysteriously linked pair of young women find their daily lives pre-empted by a strange boudoir melodrama that plays itself out in a hallucinatory parallel reality. An undisputed classic of the French New Wave, Jacques Rivette's Celine and Julie Go Boating is a delightful movie about the spiritual journey of a pair of young women, told with a playful approach to the cinematic form. A masterpiece of cinematic creativity, Rivette, the same mind behind 1969's L'amour fou, effortlessly draws the viewer into the whimsical world of the titular protagonists.

title: Interstellar
description: In Earth's future, a global crop blight and second Dust Bowl are slowly rendering the planet uninhabitable. Professor Brand (Michael Caine), a brilliant NASA physicist, is working on plans to save mankind by transporting Earth's population to a new home via a wormhole. But first, Brand must send former NASA pilot Cooper (Matthew McConaughey) and a team of researchers through the wormhole and across the galaxy to find out which of three planets could be mankind's new home.

title: DEMOLITION / CHAIQIAN / 拆·迁
description: Using a waist-high camera pointed at the ground and a drone that follows above, Nadav Assor’s GROUND EFFECT takes its name from the phenomenon by which drones and helicopters, in the process of mapping the environment, alter the landscape by displacing the ground’s surface. The objective visual recording thus becomes subjective in its effect on the land. Merging the camera footage into one, Assor points out the unique flaws and irreconcilability of objective and subjective ways of perceiving. Likewise, J.P. Sniadecki’s DEMOLITION / CHAIQIAN, produced in association with the Harvard Sensory Ethnography Lab, shakes loose a firm cinematic sense of perception. Shot over the course of three weeks and following a group of migrant demolition workers and city dwellers in Chengdu, China, DEMOLITION / CHAIQIAN imbues heavy demolition equipment with awkwardness and humor and turns cameras on cameras, all while a city is disappearing underfoot amidst a sonic tank of grinding metal, bursting concrete, and electronic beeps. Conversely, in Viktoria Schmid’s W O W (KODAK), structures reappear as demolished portions of the Rochester Kodak factory emerge from towering dust clouds, rhyming with the Lumière brothers’ DEMOLITION D’UN MUR made over a century prior. Preceded by: Viktoria Schmid W O W (KODAK) 2018, 2 min, 35mm-to-DCP Nadav Assor GROUND EFFECT 2016, 14 min, digital Total running time: ca. 85 min.

title: L'Amour braque
description: Screenings of L'Amour braque will feature a video introduction from writer and film historian, Samm Deighan. Intended as a homage to…

title: SURVIVING EDGED WEAPONS
description:
Originally produced as a police training video, the film demonstrates the dangers posed by knives and other handheld weapons through a mix of reenactments, interviews, and real-world case studies. Officers, medical professionals, and survivors recount violent encounters while the film breaks down how quickly ordinary situations can escalate into deadly confrontations.
Its reputation comes largely from the strange collision between instructional seriousness and unintentionally surreal presentation that feels like a cross between
Killing of America
and
Deadbeat at Dawn
. Detached narration, abrupt tonal shifts, and graphic practical demonstrations give it an uncanny quality that has transformed it from niche training material into a cult object of fascination.

title: You Can’t Take It with You             / Mr. Deeds Goes to Town
description: Academy Award® winner James Stewart (1940 Best Actor, The Philadelphia Story and 1985 Honorary Oscar®), Jean Arthur, Academy Award® winner Lionel Barrymore (1931 Best Actor, A Free Soul ) and Edward Arnold star in this classic screwball comedy. Based on the phenomenally successful Kaufman-Hart play, You Can’t Take It With You was directed by Frank Capra and won two Academy Awards® (1938 Best Picture, Best Director) and garnered five more nominations. It was Capra’s third Oscar® for directing. Arthur stars as Alice Sycamore, the stable family member of an offbeat clan of free spirits who falls for Stewart, the down-to-earth son of a snooty, wealthy family. Amidst a backdrop of confusion, the two very different families rediscover the simple joys of life. (Sony Pictures)

title: Preschool Pictures: The Smeds and the Smoos (U)
Lenny
description: Controversial comedian Lenny Bruce (Dustin Hoffman) begins his career telling bad jokes to bored audiences in the 1950s, but can't repress his desire to unleash edgier material. When he does, he begins a one-man campaign to break down social hypocrisy, and his groundbreaking stage act propels him to cult-hero status. When authorities ban Lenny's act for obscenity, he begins a downward spiral of drugs, sex and debt, aided by his bombshell wife, a stripper named Honey (Valerie Perrine).

title: How to Marry a Millionaire
description: Schatze, Pola, and Loco (Lauren Bacall, Marilyn Monroe, Betty Grable) are Manhattan models on a mission to marry rich husbands. Although they set their sights on Vanderbilts and Rockefellers, their plans go awry when they become attracted to men who look to be penniless. How to Marry a Millionaire was released at the end of Monroe’s breakout year, having starred in Gentlemen Prefer Blondes and Niagara in 1953. description: A group of high-end professional thieves start to feel the heat from the LAPD when they unknowingly leave a verbal clue at their latest heist. Original Cut from a 35mm print.

title: Your Name [Kimi no Na wa.]
description: Two teenagers share a profound, magical connection upon discovering they are swapping bodies. Things manage to become even more complicated when the boy and girl decide to meet in person.

description: Ex-villain Gal Dove (Ray Winstone) has served his time behind bars and is blissfully retired to a Spanish villa paradise with a wife he adores. The idyll is shattered by the arrival of his gangster nemesis Don Logan (Ben Kingsley), intent on persuading Gal to return to London for one last big job. title: The World of Jacques Demy
description: Hollywood has had its fair share of power couples; husband and wife duos that have each enjoyed illustrious careers in the film industry. In France, one of the most noteworthy marital unions occurred when Jacques Demy and Agnès Varda tied the knot in 1962. Distinguished filmmakers in their own right, the couple enjoyed nearly 30 years together until Demy died in 1990. Following his death, Varda constructed a documentary paying tribute to the work of her husband and highlighting his place in the history of film.

title: FLESHTONE
description:
A painter named Matthew Greco, fascinated by death and violence, becomes involved with a woman he meets through a phone-sex line. When he discovers a mutilated body that appears to be hers, he is drawn into a mysterious murder investigation where the victim’s identity, the motive, and the truth behind the crime become increasingly uncertain.
A dark erotic mystery thriller from director Harry Hurwitz, the film blends psychological obsession, crime, and noir elements with a distinctly early-1990s direct-to-video atmosphere. Led by Martin Kemp, it explores themes of voyeurism, fantasy, and the blurred line between desire and danger.

title: NO OTHER LAND
description: Rather than engendering solidarity and empathy through the depiction of destruction of social and material Palestinian life in the present tense, Cynthia Madansky’s STILL LIFE chooses instead to take spectators on a tour of the Occupied Territories after the bulldozers have rumbled through and the bombs have fallen. Hanging its power on aftermath, STILL LIFE reaches instead for a set of festering implications and associations triggered via images, musical composition, and spoken questions. Like many of the other films in this series, NO OTHER LAND preserves in the visual archive what will likely be lost. Shot over the course of five years and by a collective of four directors from Palestine and Israel, NO OTHER LAND shocks in its immediacy and palpable danger as an SOS call from Masafer Yatta, a front line of the Palestinian struggle. Preceded by: Cynthia Madansky STILL LIFE 2004, 15 min, Super-8mm-to-digital. Sound design by Zeena Parkins. Total running time: ca. 110 min.
director: Yuval Abraham, Basel Adra, Hamdan Ballal, and Rachel Szor

title: Never Watching Movies & Claire Harrison present CAR WASH
description: Join Never Watching Movies and Claire Harrison (usually found at Category H film club) for an evening screening of CAR WASH (1976). Follow the daily life of Dee-Luxe Car Wash employees, a tight-knit team who make the most of their minimum wage job, meeting eccentric individuals passing through the w...

title: THE MIRACLE WORKER
description: Academy Awards went to Best Actress Anne Bancroft and Best Supporting Actress Patty Duke for their moving portrayals of Annie Sullivan and her remarkable blind and deaf pupil, Helen Keller.

title: VALENTIN NOUJAÏM PGM 2: RE-TELLING
description: RE-TELLING: OUR GRANDMOTHERS HAVE KNOWN Valentin Noujaïm BEFORE SHE FORGETS HELIOPOLIS / AVANT D’OUBLIER HELIOPOLIS 2018, 23 min, digital. In French with English subtitles. “My family have begun to forget their Egyptian roots and, on asking my grandmother Malo to recount the first part of her life in Cairo, I am confronted by the memories of an exiled Arabic woman, lost in a troubled sea of memories, soon to be erased by the passage of time.” –Valentin Noujaïm Darryl Daley YOULOGY / NO GHOSTS 2025, 8 min, digital “YOULOGY / NO GHOSTS explores cyclical motifs of arrival and departure through the artist’s grandmother’s migration to the United Kingdom and her posthumous return to Jamaica, creating a transcendental frame where memory and time merge. In this speculative space, the film navigates beyond the confines of mortality, reimagining a future where inherited stories resist linearity.” –THIRD HORIZON FILM FESTIVAL Barbara Hammer OPTIC NERVE 1985, 16 min, 16mm “[A] powerful personal reflection on family and aging. Hammer employs filmed footage which, through optical printing and editing, is layered and manipulated to create a compelling meditation on her visit to her grandmother in a nursing home. The sense of sight becomes a constantly evolving process of reseeing images retrieved from the past and fused into the eternal present of the projected image. Hammer has lent a new voice to the long tradition of personal meditation in the avant-garde of the American independent cinema.” –John Hanhardt, WHITNEY MUSEUM OF AMERICAN ART Razan AlSalah YOUR FATHER WAS BORN 100 YEARS OLD, AND SO WAS THE NAKBA 2017, 7 min, digital. In Arabic with English subtitles. “She looks down at her virtual ghost marked with an X. ‘If I were walking, I would have found it, even if it’s not here anymore.’ Oum Amin, a Palestinian grandmother, returns to her hometown Haifa through Google Maps Streetview – today, the only way she can see Palestine. The film consists of images from Google Street View accompanied by an imaginary voiceover written by the artist, that of her grandmother who was never able to return to her hometown in Palestine. This invented memory, narrated in voiceover, is nevertheless set in a real colonial context. In this pixelated, stroboscopic landscape, archival images narrating British and Israeli colonization appear.” –Cinéma du Réel Caroline Monnet IKWÉ 2009, 5 min, digital. In Cree and French with English subtitles. “IKWÉ is an experimental film that weaves the narrative of one woman’s (IKWÉ) intimate thoughts with the teachings of her grandmother, the Moon, creating a surreal narrative experience that communicates the power of thoughts and personal reflection. Made by Anishinaabe artist Caroline Monnet, the film reflects the intergenerational transmission of Indigenous knowledge.” –WINNIPEG FILM GROUP / NATIONAL BOARD OF CANADA Jean-Pierre Bekolo GRANDMA’S GRAMMAR / LA GRAMMAIRE DE MA GRAND’MERE 1996, 8 min, digital. In French with English subtitles. “An inherited lesson from Djibril Diop Mambéty’s grandmother is transmitted through Jean-Pierre Bekolo’s chronicle of their conversation. Creating a Pan-African exchange, the Cameroonian Bekolo listens to the Senegalese Mambéty root his cinema in his grandmother’s storytelling – a narrative form of returns and repetitions, of continuation and reinvention.” –Yasmina Price Shenny De Los Ángeles & Amanda Morell (iiritu) FLORINDA’S DAUGHTER / HIJA DE FLORINDA 2024, 12 min, digital. In English and Spanish with English subtitles. “Through a series of black-and-white tableaux, this poetry film follows the journey of Young Naomi in Everglades, Florida. She learns from Florinda, her grandmother, about the ancestral practices of caring for the land and nurturing grief in the face of environmental challenges. As the story unfolds, we grow to understand Florinda’s indigenous teachings of controlled burns and the importance of embracing fire rather than suppressing it. As the prescribed burns ignite from Florinda’s hands, an archival portal is birthed.” –BROOKLYN ACADEMY OF MUSIC Total running time: ca. 85 min. Followed by a conversation between Yasmina Price and writer, editor, and critic Jessica Lynne!

title: Far from Heaven
description: A suburban housewife discovers her husband has a secret life, only to find herself becoming emotionally involved with another man, in writer-director Todd Haynes’s sincere and expertly crafted homage to the 1950s melodramas of Douglas Sirk. Best Actress nominee Julianne Moore gives a perfectly pitched lead performance, with strong support from Dennis Quaid, Dennis Haysbert, Patricia Clarkson and Viola Davis. The film also received nominations for Haynes’s sensitive screenplay, Edward Lachman’s autumnal cinematography, and the gorgeously old-fashioned score by Elmer Bernstein. One of the film’s producers is Haynes’s longtime collaborator Christine Vachon, one of this year’s Governors Awards winners (with longtime filmmaking partner Pamela Koffler) for her remarkable and groundbreaking career.

title: The Virgin Suicides
description: A group of male friends become obsessed with five mysterious sisters who are sheltered by their strict, religious parents.

title: LAH: 450 XL A Silent Movie (cert tbc)
Paris, Texas
description: A disheveled man who wanders out of the desert, Travis Henderson (Harry Dean Stanton) seems to have no idea who he is. When a stranger manages to contact his brother, Walt (Dean Stockwell), Travis is awkwardly reunited with his sibling. Travis has been missing for years, and his presence unsettles Walt and his family, which also includes Travis's own son, Hunter (Hunter Carson). Soon Travis must confront his wife, Jane (Nastassja Kinski), and try to put his life back together.

title: Yumeji
description: Following the life of Japanese artist and poet Yumeji Takehisa through the imagining of an encounter with a beautiful widow with a dark past.

title: IN THE COLD OF THE NIGHT
description:
A high‑profile fashion photographer named Scott Bruin is plagued by a series of increasingly disturbing nightmares in which he appears to attack and kill a mysterious woman. When that woman begins to step out of his dreams and into his waking life, Scott must confront whether his visions are merely fantasies or harbingers of something more sinister and real.
This 1990 erotic thriller blends psychological mystery with late‑night cable ambience and surreal dream logic. Its mix of neon‑soaked visuals, uneasy tension, and uncanny mood make it a standout example of early‑90s genre cinema that sits somewhere between noir, nightmare, and sleazy intrigue.

title: STILL LIFE / 三峡好人
description: If Jia Zhangke’s breakout film PLATFORM (2000) was about the destruction of China’s social fabric as it transitioned from Mao to Deng Xiaoping, then Jia’s 2006 Golden Lion winner STILL LIFE focuses on the physical destruction of the built environment as the country ventures through another epochal shift. Like Ou Ning’s MEISHI STREET, STILL LIFE is firmly located during what Western observers routinely note as the era of a “rising China.” A few years after the country’s admittance to the WTO, a couple years before Beijing hosted the 2008 Olympics, and during a time of rising GDP, STILL LIFE asks, in literal terms, whether a rising tide indeed lifts all boats. Shot on location in Fengjie, a town along the Yangtze River in central China, the film centers on two people as they search for their spouses in the city, slowly being demolished to make way for the Three Gorges Dam. Slated to be flooded by the dam’s reservoir, the town is replete with hand painted red lines on the sides of buildings that indicate the imminent water levels, offering a stark warning for those below the line to get out while they can. Like Pedro Costa’s IN VANDA’S ROOM, STILL LIFE is filmed on digital video, lending it not only a documentary aesthetic (emblematic of the Urban Generation of Chinese independent filmmakers at the time), but one of uncanny immediacy. Jia, embracing the xianchang spirit of on-the-ground filmmaking, has argued that the documentarian must allow themself to be “seared” by the immediate present. The traces of the people and buildings of Fengjie, though now relocated and demolished, respectively, become irrevocably imprinted on STILL LIFE and its maker.

title: GUMMO
description: With strains of his nihilistic youth-culture script for Larry Clark’s KIDS, Harmony Korine’s directorial debut moves out of the city to wander the post-apocalyptic fallout of a suburban Midwestern landscape recently ravaged by a tornado. Weaving between the day-to-day lives of various poverty-stricken small-town outcasts, GUMMO’s scattershot structure and varied shooting styles present a collage of American themes on the precipice of an unpredictable new millennium, ultimately yielding a movie that Gus Van Sant called “both bracingly realistic and hauntingly dreamlike.”

title: You Can’t Take It with You             / Mr. Deeds Goes to Town
description: Academy Award® winner James Stewart (1940 Best Actor, The Philadelphia Story and 1985 Honorary Oscar®), Jean Arthur, Academy Award® winner Lionel Barrymore (1931 Best Actor, A Free Soul ) and Edward Arnold star in this classic screwball comedy. Based on the phenomenally successful Kaufman-Hart play, You Can’t Take It With You was directed by Frank Capra and won two Academy Awards® (1938 Best Picture, Best Director) and garnered five more nominations. It was Capra’s third Oscar® for directing. Arthur stars as Alice Sycamore, the stable family member of an offbeat clan of free spirits who falls for Stewart, the down-to-earth son of a snooty, wealthy family. Amidst a backdrop of confusion, the two very different families rediscover the simple joys of life. (Sony Pictures)

title: April X
description: When his twin sister April (Lilly Krug) goes missing, Bax (Connor Storrie) searches every corner of their futuristic, post-Soviet cityscape to find her, ultimately descending into madness.

title: The Dirties
description: The line between reality and fiction starts to blur when two best friends start making a movie about getting revenge on bullies.

title: Interstellar
description: In Earth's future, a global crop blight and second Dust Bowl are slowly rendering the planet uninhabitable. Professor Brand (Michael Caine), a brilliant NASA physicist, is working on plans to save mankind by transporting Earth's population to a new home via a wormhole. But first, Brand must send former NASA pilot Cooper (Matthew McConaughey) and a team of researchers through the wormhole and across the galaxy to find out which of three planets could be mankind's new home.

title: Nirvanna the Band the Show the Movie
description: When their plan to book a show at the Rivoli goes horribly wrong, Matt and Jay accidentally travel back to the year 2008.

title: In-I In Motion + Q&A with Juliette Binoche
Cinema Paradiso [Nuovo Cinema Paradiso]
description: A winner of awards across the world including Best Foreign Language Film Oscar, 5 BAFTA Awards including Best Actor, Original Screenplay and Score, the Grand Prize of the Jury at the Cannes Film Festival and many more. Giuseppe Tornatore's loving homage to the cinema tells the story of Salvatore, a successful film director, returning home for the funeral of Alfredo, his old friend who was the projectionist at the local cinema throughout his childhood. Soon memories of his first love affair with the beautiful Elena and all the highs and lows that shaped his life come flooding back, as Salvatore reconnects with the community he left 30 years earlier.

title: Picture This + Q&A
description: Directed by Anna Fox, Sarah Jeans and Anne Parisio, Picture This is a heartwarming portrait of three groups of women in Edinburgh, Farnham and London. The women are from refugee and migrant communities and a women’s refuge, as they have all had to leave their own countries or homes because of war, their sexuality or to escape abusive relationships. Professor Anna Fox, an internationally renowned photographer and university lecturer introduces us to the different participants as they receive training to use photography to reinterpret their experiences and create moving images. Through a series of industry visits, industry partners and visiting lectures, Anna introduces the women to aspects of the industry with the aim of helping them to develop future careers in the photography industries. Picture This , is an output of Putting Ourselves in The Picture – Part 2 Engaging With Industry which has been funded through the Arts and Humanities Research Council (AHRC) and the University for The Creative Arts (UCA). The project is part of Fast Forward: Women in Photography, which was established in 2014 at UCA Farnham, UK. Fast Forward is a world wide research network that gathers and disseminates new knowledge about past and present female photographers, with the aim of empowering women through engaging in debate, discourse and dissemination about these often hidden histories. The screening will be followed by a Q&A with the directors and participants.

title: The Terminator
description: Disguised as a human, a cyborg assassin known as a Terminator (Arnold Schwarzenegger) travels from 2029 to 1984 to kill Sarah Connor (Linda Hamilton). Sent to protect Sarah is Kyle Reese (Michael Biehn), who divulges the coming of Skynet, an artificial intelligence system that will spark a nuclear holocaust. Sarah is targeted because Skynet knows that her unborn son will lead the fight against them. With the virtually unstoppable Terminator in hot pursuit, she and Kyle attempt to escape. 40th Anniversary restoration from a 4K film scan of the 35mm negative and a new Dolby Atmos mix with final sound and picture approved by director James Cameron. title: IN VANDA’S ROOM / NO QUARTO DA VANDA
description: The second in his Fontainhas trilogy, IN VANDA’S ROOM follows heroin addict Vanda Duarte and a group of struggling slum dwellers as they try to make a life amid the demolition of their Lisbon neighborhood. Between Vanda’s raucous coughing fits and the clicks of her butane lighter, Costa’s extreme long takes, filmed in austere digital video, capture the sound of her built environs collapsing around her. Unlike the Barcelona neighborhood in EN CONSTRUCCIÓN, though, Fontainhas was wiped from the map by city officials, irredeemable in the eyes of the state, its inhabitants moved elsewhere. Today, it no longer stands, but remains embalmed in the images of Costa’s film. IN VANDA’S ROOM probes the limit of what cinema is and is capable of, not only in its content, which is bleak and harrowing to be sure, but in its form. Like many films in this series, it is uninterested in the distinction between fiction and documentary, choosing instead to capture life in its essence by whatever means necessary. André Bazin wrote that photography, and by extension cinema, satisfied the deep need that man had for an image that was not an approximation, but was the object itself, “freed from the conditions of time and space that govern it.” Sometimes, truth must be freed from the conditions of the objectively real: Costa proclaimed that he filmed some scenes multiple times until they “became fluidly represented and detached of any melodramatic tone.” Often, truth requires some coaxing.

title: NARROW ROOMS: JERKER
description: In a San Francisco apartment, in 1985, Bert is just about to fall asleep when a stranger named J.R. calls. “You hard?” he asks Bert, and the two begin a hot and heavy phone sex session that soon turns into a nightly routine. Over the span of a year, we watch as Bert (Tom Wagner) and J.R. (Joseph Stachura) explore their fantasies, get each other off, and forge a deeper connection that allows them to open up to each other about their fears and sorrows surrounding the AIDS epidemic, all without ever meeting face to face. Playwright Robert Chesley wryly called his groundbreaking 1986 play JERKER “a pornographic elegy with redeeming social value and a hymn to the queer men of San Francisco,” which perhaps sought to preempt the inevitable criticism and censorship of the play’s unabashedly sex-positive dialogue. Hugh Harrison’s smart, rarely seen 1991 adaptation combines the rich, raunchy text of Chesley’s play with the shot-on-video aesthetics of late 1980s gay adult films, making us feel as if we’re watching an especially well-written Jeff Stryker or Joey Stefano movie. Help us celebrate the 40th anniversary of JERKER’s theatrical premiere with this very special screening.

Originally released in 2003 and premiered at PCC, Girl Skateboards' YEAH RIGHT redefined what was possible in skateboard filmmaking. Combining groundbreaking parts from an all-star team with Spike Jonze and Ty Evans' unforgettable direction, innovative visual effects and iconic soundtrack. More than 20 years on, it's still as funny, inventive and inspiring as ever, and rarely seen on the big screen.

Another Terminator, the revamped T-800 (Arnold Schwarzenegger), has been sent back to protect the boy. During his stay in the Bronx, Keong befriends a neighbour kid and beats up some neighbourhood thugs who cause problems at the market. Director Wes Craven and screenwriter Kevin Williamson mix keenly self-aware wit with modern scares to reinvent the slasher mold and reinvigorate the genre for a new generation, launching a sensation with their smash hit Scream .

title: How to Marry a Millionaire
description: Schatze, Pola, and Loco (Lauren Bacall, Marilyn Monroe, Betty Grable) are Manhattan models on a mission to marry rich husbands. Although they set their sights on Vanderbilts and Rockefellers, their plans go awry when they become attracted to men who look to be penniless. How to Marry a Millionaire was released at the end of Monroe’s breakout year, having starred in Gentlemen Prefer Blondes and Niagara in 1953. The film is notable as the first to be completed in CinemaScope, and Monroe had such broad appeal that 20th Century-Fox used her to advertise this new widescreen format: a slogan above an image of Marilyn claimed she was “Big as life and a million times more fun in Cinemascope!”

title: Akira
description: Iconic and game-changing, AKIRA is the definitive anime masterpiece! Katsuhiro Otomo's landmark cyberpunk classic obliterated the boundaries of Japanese animation and forced the world to look into the future. AKIRA's arrival shattered traditional thinking, creating space for future generations of ground-breaking movies. July, 1988 - World War III breaks loose. Then, in 2019, in megalopolis Tokyo...As the leader of a group of young robust delinquents, Kaneda spent his nights tearing through the urban wastes, racing his motorbike against rival groups. One night while riding with his gang, his friend Tetsuo suddenly encounters a strange boy - the product of human experimentation and is injured in the ensuing crash. Shortly thereafter, a military squadron appears on the scene to take the boy and Tetsuo away to an army research facility. Determined to free Tetsuo from capture, Kaneda sneaks into the army research lab. However, a regimen of extreme experimental procedures has awakened a new power in his friend, and now he is consumed by madness..
